fool.name: The Fool
fool.meaning_upright: The Fool is the card of the starting point, where every road is still open and you are not yet weighed down by expectations or fear. It invites you to step forward with a light heart, curious like a child facing the unknown. You may be standing before a big decision, a journey, a project or a completely different chapter of life. The universe seems to whisper that you do not need every answer before you are allowed to begin. Trust your intuition, stay open, and accept that small mistakes are part of the journey. Still, the spirit of adventure is most beautiful when paired with a little awareness: look at your feet before you step, so trust does not turn into carelessness. This is a time to try, to learn, and to be freely yourself.
fool.meaning_reversed: When the Fool appears reversed, the spirit of adventure can lean in two directions: either you are acting too hastily, or you are standing at the edge of the cliff without daring to step. In the first case, impulsiveness makes you overlook warning signs and bet on something you have not thought through. In the second, fear of failure or worry about how others will see you holds you back and lets opportunities pass. The card asks you to find a balance between recklessness and delay. Ask yourself what you are running from, or what you are afraid of. Review your plan, prepare what you need, and then move forward with awareness. One small but conscious step is usually better than a blind leap.

love.upright: In love, The Fool brings a fresh, excited feeling, like the first days of getting to know someone. If you are single, you may meet someone unexpectedly or open yourself to experiences you have never tried. If you are in a relationship, this is a time to do something new together and keep a playful, light-hearted spirit.
love.reversed: Reversed, the card warns you not to rush into a relationship on a passing wave of excitement, nor to avoid commitment out of fear of losing your freedom. You may be naive about the other person's intentions, or you may not yet be serious about your own feelings. Slow down for a beat and understand what you truly need.

career.upright: In your career, this is a signal for a new beginning: a new job, a new direction, or a creative idea nobody has tried yet. You are encouraged to experiment, learn from the position of a beginner, and keep your curiosity. A flexible, exploratory environment suits you right now.
career.reversed: Reversed, you may be making a career decision without enough preparation, or hesitating for too long while an opportunity is knocking. Check your skills, information and risks. Do not quit or accept a job on a burst of inspiration alone without a clear plan.

study.upright: In study, this is the time to begin a completely new subject, field or skill. Keep a beginner's mind, dare to ask questions and to make mistakes; curiosity will take you further than perfection.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be jumping into a direction of study without looking into it properly, or putting things off for fear of starting. Take a little time to define your goal and your path before signing up for another course.

finance.upright: In finances, The Fool suggests a new opportunity or a new way of thinking about money: a small project, a learning investment, or a change in spending habits. Keep an open mind, but remember to set limits, and only try with an amount you could accept losing if the result is not what you hoped.
finance.reversed: Reversed, the card warns about impulsive spending or financial decisions made without research. You may be carried away by an opportunity that sounds very attractive. Pause, read carefully, ask someone knowledgeable, and set clear limits before putting in money or committing.

mind.upright: For well-being and energy, the card encourages gentle movement, trying a new habit, getting out into nature and letting your mind relax. Play, laughter and a feeling of lightness are also forms of self-care. For specific concerns, ask a healthcare professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are draining your energy through a lack of planning, or ignoring your body's signals because you are busy. Pay attention to your sleep, your daily rhythm and careless habits. If something worries you, do not put off seeing a doctor.

fool.symbolism: The young man stands at the edge of a cliff with his eyes raised to the sky instead of looking at his feet, showing complete trust and optimism toward the unknown. The bright white sun behind him symbolizes purity and fresh energy. The small bag on his stick shows he carries only what he needs; his baggage is experience that has not yet taken shape. The white rose in his left hand stands for pure desire, and the little dog at his feet is a loyal companion who also seems to remind him to stay alert. The snowy mountains in the distance hint that the road ahead is long. The card carries the number 0, the number of unformed possibility, and is linked to the element of Air and the planet Uranus, symbols of breakthrough and freedom.
fool.miu: Meow~ Sometimes jumping first and thinking later is fine… but do check whether there is a puddle under your feet. Cats hate getting wet!

magician.name: The Magician
magician.meaning_upright: The Magician is the card of the power to turn intention into reality. You have the tools, skills and resources to begin; all you need is focus and purposeful action. The card says that the line between wanting something and achieving it often lies in your determination and in how you use what you already have. This is a good time to launch a project, communicate clearly, show your talent and trust your abilities. You can connect ideas with reality, and the unseen with concrete action. Define your goal, gather your strength in one direction, and get to work. Real magic is not a miracle but clarity, discipline and belief shown through every small task.
magician.meaning_reversed: When the Magician is reversed, your talent may not be used in the right way. You may be scattering your energy, doubting yourself, or waiting for a perfect moment without starting. It is also possible that someone is using their cleverness to manipulate, or that you are painting an image of yourself that goes beyond reality. The card asks you to check your motives: are you using your abilities to build or to hide? Be honest about your goals, focus on one thing first, and be careful with promises that sound too good. When you are sincere and clear, your energy will return.

love.upright: In love, the Magician shows charm, initiative and a captivating way of communicating. You know how to express yourself and to create what you want in a relationship. If you are single, this is a time to shine and start conversations. If you are in a relationship, say clearly what you need and act together to refresh your connection.
love.reversed: Reversed, the card warns about pretty words without sincerity, or about hiding your true feelings. There may be subtle manipulation or unclear expectations. Watch actions more than words, and ask yourself whether you are being genuine.

career.upright: In your career, this is a very positive card for starting a business, presenting, creating and leading projects. Your skills are at a point where they can produce clear results. Make use of your network and the tools at hand, and present your value with confidence.
career.reversed: Reversed, you may be doing too many things at once, lacking direction, or underestimating yourself. Be careful of an environment where people are not honest. Return to one concrete goal and prove your ability through real results.

study.upright: In study, you have the tools and the ability to turn knowledge into results. This is a good time to practise, do small projects and present what you have learned.
study.reversed: Reversed, your knowledge may be scattered or used in the wrong place. Focus on one goal, avoid studying only to get by, and do not overrate or underrate your own ability.

finance.upright: In finances, the Magician suggests you can create extra income from your skills, or manage your resources skillfully. Make a concrete plan and use what you already have. Caution is the foundation, but taking initiative is also necessary.
finance.reversed: Reversed, the card warns about get-rich-quick offers, tricks or information that lacks transparency. You may also be spending without a clear purpose. Verify your sources and avoid commitments beyond your understanding.

mind.upright: For your body's energy, the Magician reminds you that health starts with intention and steady action. Build a concrete habit and focus on one small goal such as sleeping on time or moving more. For medical matters, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests scattered energy, an overloaded mind or a lack of discipline in your habits. Cut back on what is unnecessary, simplify your schedule and pay attention to your body's signs of tiredness.

magician.symbolism: The magician stands with one hand raised to the sky holding a wand and the other pointing to the earth, showing the principle of 'as above, so below': he is the bridge between spirit and matter. On the table before him lie the four suits of the deck, wands, cups, swords and coins, meaning every tool is within his reach. The horizontal figure eight above his head is the infinity symbol, pointing to endlessly flowing energy. The red cloak stands for passion, while the white robe beneath is the purity of intention. The red roses and white lilies around him show desire and wisdom blooming together. The snake biting its tail around his belt suggests the cycle of life. The card belongs to the element of Air and is linked to Mercury, the god of communication and change.
magician.miu: The secret of magic is… practice! It took Miu three whole years to pull dried fish out of this hat.

priestess.name: The High Priestess
priestess.meaning_upright: The High Priestess invites you to pause and listen to the voice within. Some answers do not come from analysis but from stillness, from a feeling that is vague yet certain in your heart. The card shows you are at the threshold of something not yet spoken: a secret, a new awareness, or a process unfolding quietly. This is not a time for hasty action but for observing, reflecting and trusting your intuition. Write in a journal, meditate or spend time alone to hear more clearly what you feel. Deep understanding will appear when you are patient enough. Not everything needs to be explained right away; some truths only show themselves when you let them arrive at their own pace.
priestess.meaning_reversed: When reversed, your connection with your intuition may be clouded by outside noise, anxiety or relying too much on logic. You may be ignoring a clear sign simply because you are not ready to face it. The card can also hint at hidden information, secrets or a lack of transparency around you. Turn down the noise, find stillness again and ask yourself what you are avoiding. Do not trust the surface too quickly; look more closely. If it feels hard to hear your inner voice, begin with simple things like deep breathing or a walk alone.

love.upright: In love, the card shows a relationship with emotional depth, where understanding needs few words. Something may be left unsaid, or you may be quietly sensing a connection. Trust your intuition when you look at the other person, and take time to observe before opening up completely.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests something is hidden or there is a lack of openness between two people. You may be brushing aside a feeling of unease inside you. Talk honestly and gently, and do not guess too much about what the other person is thinking.

career.upright: At work, rely on deep expertise and observation instead of rushing to act. This is a good time for research, study, work that calls for subtlety, or behind-the-scenes work. Important information may not be fully shared yet, so be patient.
career.reversed: Reversed, information at work may be unclear, or you may not be following what your gut tells you. Be careful with office politics and unspoken understandings. Ask clearly and gather more data before deciding.

study.upright: In study, intuition and stillness are helping you understand more deeply. Read carefully, reflect, and let knowledge settle instead of chasing speed; what is left unsaid in your materials is also worth noticing.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be ignoring your inner voice, or memorizing without really understanding. Ask again about the parts that are still vague and do not hesitate to ask a teacher or classmate to explain.

finance.upright: Finances now call for quiet consideration. Research carefully, do not rush to commit, and listen to your feelings about investments or spending. There may be factors not yet revealed, so learn more before you act.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you lack information or are making money decisions without truly understanding. Be careful with vague terms, check documents closely and do not dismiss your own sense of unease.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card encourages quiet time, meditation, journaling and listening to your body. Emotional balance comes from allowing yourself to rest. For specific concerns, consult a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are ignoring your body's signals or holding feelings in. Give yourself time to slow down, share what you are carrying with someone you trust, and do not delay a health check when you need one.

priestess.symbolism: The priestess sits between a black and a white pillar marked B and J, hinting at the two pillars of Solomon's temple and symbolizing duality: dark and light, hidden and revealed. She sits before a veil embroidered with pomegranates, a symbol of fertility and concealed knowledge, which separates the visible world from the unseen. The scroll in her hand reads TORA, partly hidden, saying that knowledge is revealed only in part. The crown of three moons and the crescent moon at her feet tie her to the moon's cycles and to intuition. The solar cross on her chest stands for balance. The card belongs to the element of Water and is linked to the Moon, which rules emotion, dreams and the subconscious.
priestess.miu: Shh… cats always know before it rains. You know too, you just have not wanted to listen.

empress.name: The Empress
empress.meaning_upright: The Empress is the image of abundance, nurturing and life in full bloom. The card invites you to connect with your senses, with nature and with the beauty around you. This is a favorable stage for creating, caring for what you love and letting things grow at their natural pace. A project, a relationship or an idea may be slowly ripening. The card also speaks of generosity, gentleness and allowing yourself to enjoy life. You do not need to force anything; you only need to plant seeds, water them and be patient. Appreciate your body, make time for joy and show your feelings sincerely. True wealth is feeling that you have enough and being able to share it.
empress.meaning_reversed: When the Empress is reversed, nurturing energy can tip out of balance: you may look after others so much that you forget yourself, or on the other hand lack creative drive and feel drained. Sometimes the card points to dependence, overindulgence, or control under the name of care. Ask yourself whether you feel full from within. Take time for self-care, reconnect with nature and allow yourself to rest. When you are nourished, creativity will return naturally. Set healthy limits in the way you give.

love.upright: In love, the Empress brings warmth, closeness and sincere care. The relationship may be blossoming or moving toward steadier steps. If you are single, your gentleness makes it easy to attract others. Give love, and let yourself be loved too.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests imbalance: one person gives too much, or the relationship becomes suffocating. You may feel under-appreciated. Express your needs and do not lose yourself for someone else.

career.upright: In your career, this is a time of creativity, growth and gradual harvest. Work involving care, art, design or building a good environment for others is favored. Work steadily and patiently, and let your project ripen naturally.
career.reversed: Reversed, you may be stuck for ideas or overworking without recognition. Rest, find fresh inspiration and review your boundaries at work; do not take on the role of caring for everyone.

study.upright: In study, a comfortable environment and taking care of yourself help learning bloom. Creative subjects, the arts and people-centered fields are especially favored; study steadily without pushing yourself.
study.reversed: Reversed, your studies may be disturbed by emotions or by taking things too easily. Rebuild balanced eating, sleeping and study routines, and do not wait for inspiration to open a book.

finance.upright: In finances, the card often suggests gradual stability and abundance. You may enjoy the fruit of earlier effort. Spend with purpose on what brings joy and security, while continuing to plant long-term seeds.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests overspending to soothe emotions, or worrying about scarcity even when things are fine. Review your budget, tell needs from wants, and do not become financially dependent on someone else without clarity.

mind.upright: For general well-being, the Empress encourages healthy eating, gentle movement, time near nature and appreciating your body. Rest and joy are medicine too. For specific conditions, consult a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are neglecting your basic needs or using food or shopping to soothe your feelings. Rebuild self-care habits from small things and seek support if you need it.

empress.symbolism: The empress sits on a soft cushioned seat amid a field of ripe wheat and a green forest, showing the abundance of nature. Her gown, patterned with pomegranates, suggests fertility and the ability to flourish. The crown of twelve stars stands for twelve months and twelve zodiac signs, tying her to the cycles of heaven and earth. The scepter in her hand shows soft yet firm power. The heart-shaped shield with the symbol of Venus beside her stresses love and beauty. The stream flowing behind her is an endless source of life. The card carries the number 3, the number of creativity, and is linked to Venus and the element of Earth.
empress.miu: A good meal, an afternoon nap in the sun… Miu calls that the highest kind of magic.

emperor.name: The Emperor
emperor.meaning_upright: The Emperor represents order, authority and a solid foundation. The card shows that you need to, or are able to, set up a clear structure, make decisive choices and take responsibility. This is a time to use reason, discipline and long-term planning to build what you want. You may be facing a leadership role, someone in authority, or a need to set boundaries. The card encourages you to stand firm, hold your position and act in an organized way. Good authority does not come from control but from being reliable, fair and able to protect what matters. Ask yourself whether you are ready to take charge of your own life, and whether your foundation is strong enough to build on.
emperor.meaning_reversed: When the Emperor is reversed, authority may be abused or lacking. You may meet someone domineering, or you may be too rigid yourself and controlling down to the details. It may also be that you lack discipline, avoid responsibility and let things fall into disorder. The card asks you to look again at your relationship with authority: are you resisting for no reason, or imposing on others? Find the balance between flexibility and firmness. A good leader knows when to hold to principles and when to listen.

love.upright: In love, the Emperor suggests stability, commitment and a wish to build a solid future. The other person may be mature and dependable. Stay clear, responsible and respectful of boundaries, while remembering to keep some softness in how you show your feelings.
love.reversed: Reversed, the card warns about control or imposition in a relationship, or about a lack of commitment that leaves the other person insecure. Review how decisions are shared and express your needs without forcing.

career.upright: In your career, this is the card of leadership, management, organizing and building systems. You may be given more responsibility or need to set a long-term plan. Working with process, discipline and decisiveness will bring good results.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a boss or environment that is too rigid, or that you lack organization and avoid responsibility. Find ways to communicate effectively with those in authority, and set a framework for your own work.

study.upright: In study, discipline and a clear plan are the key. Make a timetable, set goals by milestones and stay serious, especially for exams or tightly structured programs.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be too rigid with yourself, or on the other hand lacking discipline. Adjust your plan to be more realistic, and do not resist rules or instructors just because you feel uncomfortable.

finance.upright: In finances, the card encourages discipline: make a budget, set long-term goals and build a stable foundation. Safety comes from a clear plan and considered decisions, not from chasing emotion.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests uncontrolled spending, or on the other hand being so strict that you miss opportunities. There may be pressure from someone in authority affecting your finances. Review your plan and keep reasonable flexibility.

mind.upright: For health, the Emperor points to building routine: regular hours, disciplined exercise and rest. The body needs structure to stay steady. For medical concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, you may be too harsh on yourself and creating stress, or lacking routine so that your well-being wobbles. Find a balance, set achievable goals and allow yourself to relax.

emperor.symbolism: The emperor sits on a stone throne carved with ram's heads, symbols of Aries and Mars, suggesting determination and pioneering energy. He wears a red robe over armor, showing action and protection, and holds the Ankh cross and an orb, symbols of life and dominion. The rocky mountains behind him hint at a solid yet barren foundation, standing for the hardness of discipline. The small river running through the mountains reminds us that even power needs a stream of feeling. The red-orange sky is the energy of fire. The card carries the number 4, the number of foundation and stability, and is linked to the element of Fire and the sign of Aries.
emperor.miu: Miu is emperor of the sofa. First law: nobody sits in the sunny spot.

hierophant.name: The Hierophant
hierophant.meaning_upright: The Hierophant is tied to tradition, shared values and structures that have stood the test of time. The card suggests you can learn from a teacher, an organization or a method that already exists instead of groping your way alone. You may be seeking guidance, wanting to belong to a community, or considering meaningful rites such as study, marriage or ceremonies. It encourages you to respect principles, patiently follow a systematic path and look for deeper meaning in conventions. At the same time, it asks you which beliefs are truly yours and which are inherited. Real knowledge is not only following along but understanding the reasons behind it.
hierophant.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the card encourages you to question old rules that no longer fit. You may want to escape a mold, find your own path, or push back against something imposed on you. On the other hand, it can warn against rebelling just for the sake of rebelling, or against organizations and guides who rely on dogma and authority. Consider what in tradition is worth keeping and what needs renewing. Freedom of thought is precious, but do not overlook the lessons that have already been gathered.

love.upright: In love, the Hierophant suggests a serious relationship leaning toward commitment, marriage or shared values. The two of you may share beliefs, family or community. Talk about what each of you holds dear to build a solid foundation.
love.reversed: Reversed, it points to a relationship outside the usual mold, or a clash over values and family expectations. You may feel hemmed in by convention. Be brave about saying what you truly want and look for a way to live honestly.

career.upright: In your career, you benefit from learning, having a mentor, following a program, or working in an organization with clear processes. Respect the rules, build your credibility and share knowledge with others.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you want to leave a rigid environment or break an old process. Consider a more flexible way of working, but first understand the rules well so that change is effective.

study.upright: In study, this is the time to follow the formal path: school, curriculum, an experienced teacher. A solid foundation and structured guidance will help more than figuring things out alone.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may want to step away from traditional learning or feel the current program does not suit you. Consider a learning style of your own, but master the basics before you break the mold.

finance.upright: In finances, the card supports a traditional, systematic approach: advice from experts, sustainable saving plans, tried-and-true options. Learn more about money from trustworthy sources.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you may want to try another path or doubt conventional advice. Research carefully, do not follow the crowd blindly, but do not ignore existing experience either.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card advises you to follow methods that have been tested, work with a trustworthy guide and keep steady habits. Being part of a community is also good for the mind. Ask a professional about any specific concern.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you want to find your own way of caring for yourself outside the usual mold. Be open but careful with methods that lack a basis, and think carefully before making big changes.

hierophant.symbolism: The pope sits between two pillars, his right hand raised in blessing with two fingers up and two down, showing the link between heaven and earth. His triple crown stands for three levels of awareness: body, mind and spirit. Two monks kneel before him in robes of roses and lilies, representing the receiving of knowledge. The two crossed keys at his feet are the keys that open the doors to the conscious and subconscious mind. The triple-crossed staff stresses sacred authority. The card carries the number 5, the number of challenge and learning, and is linked to the element of Earth and the sign of Taurus.
hierophant.miu: Miu's teacher says: 'Sleeping a full sixteen hours is what makes a true cat.' Miu always listens to the teacher.

lovers.name: The Lovers
lovers.meaning_upright: The Lovers speaks of deep connection and important choices based on your values. The card often suggests a relationship with harmony of feeling, spirit and body, while reminding you that love comes with responsibility. At a deeper level, it is the card of choosing what is true to yourself, whether that is a person, a job or a way of living. You are invited to live honestly, with your thoughts, words and actions in line. Listen to your heart but weigh it with reason too, because a truly meaningful choice is one you dare to take responsibility for. Ask yourself: what fits my core values?
lovers.meaning_reversed: When reversed, harmony may be cracking, or you are facing a choice you have not dared to confront. There may be a clash of values, a lack of honesty or a feeling of distance. You may also be choosing to meet others' expectations instead of your own voice. The card asks you to return to honesty and to look again at what you truly value. Speak plainly about your needs, talk openly, and if you are hesitating, find out what you are afraid of before deciding.

love.upright: In love, the Lovers is one of the most beautiful cards: true connection, understanding and deep commitment. You may meet someone who makes you feel in tune. Open your heart, be honest and cherish this harmony.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests discord, a lack of honesty, or standing between two romantic choices. There may be emotional distance. Talk frankly and do not choose out of fear of loneliness or pressure.

career.upright: At work, the card points to harmonious cooperation or a decision tied to values, such as choosing work that fits your passion or the right partner. Choose a place where you can live true to yourself and work with people who share your direction.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows conflict in the team, a difference of views, or having to choose between opportunities that are hard to weigh. Clarify your priorities and avoid deciding only under pressure.

study.upright: In study, you stand before an important choice such as a field, a school or a direction. Choose according to your values and real passion; studying in a group with compatible people is also favorable.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be hesitating, choosing under pressure from others, or letting romance distract you from study. Be clear about what you want before deciding.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests decisions that fit your personal values, or financial cooperation with someone you trust. Discuss openly if you share expenses, and put priority on what is truly meaningful.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of disagreement about money in a relationship, or financial choices that go against your values. Be transparent, agree on shared goals, and avoid rushing a decision while emotions run high.

mind.upright: For well-being, the Lovers reminds you to balance body and feeling, reason and heart. Healthy relationships are also a good source of energy. Choose habits that suit you. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests imbalance, stress from relationships, or long indecision that wears you out. Listen to your body and give yourself room to think more clearly and calmly.

lovers.symbolism: Two nude figures stand under the angel Raphael, showing the purity and honesty of facing each other. The woman looks up at the angel, who stands for higher awareness, while the man looks at the woman, hinting at the link between reason and the subconscious. The tree with a serpent behind the woman recalls the story of the Garden of Eden, temptation and awareness. The tree of twelve flames behind the man stands for passion and the twelve zodiac signs. A large sun shines over everything. The card carries the number 6, the number of harmony, and is linked to the element of Air and the sign of Gemini, the place of connection and choice.
lovers.miu: Fish or milk? Miu picks both. But people sometimes really do have to choose, you know.

chariot.name: The Chariot
chariot.meaning_upright: The Chariot is the card of determination and of victory through willpower. You are moving forward with a clear goal, steering the opposing pulls within yourself, such as reason and emotion, ambition and fear. The card shows that focus, self-control and discipline will help you overcome obstacles. This is a time to act instead of waiting. Decide where you are going, keep a steady hand on the reins and do not let inner conflicts pull you off course. Victory comes not from suppressing everything but from reconciling it and leading it in one direction. Trust the power of your will and keep going toward what you want.
chariot.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be losing control of your direction, or opposing forces are tearing at you and making you stall. You may be too aggressive, pushing forward without a plan, or lacking clear motivation. The card asks you to stop, review your goal and adjust your approach. Sometimes slowing down to hold the reins more steadily is better than rushing without looking at the road. Find your focus and discipline again, gently but firmly.

love.upright: In love, the Chariot suggests taking initiative, visible progress or overcoming obstacles together. You may be determined to pursue the one you love, or work toward a shared goal. Show confidence but still listen to the other person.
love.reversed: Reversed, the card warns of conflict over control or different directions in a relationship. You may be pushing too hard or swept along by emotion. Slow down, talk, and adjust together so that you head the same way.

career.upright: At work, the card signals progress, promotion or reaching a goal through effort. Stay focused, be decisive and lead your project steadily. This is a good time to compete and prove your ability.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a project veering off course, lacking direction, or conflict in the team. Review your goals, arrange your priorities and avoid working through aggression; use a clear plan instead.

study.upright: In study, willpower and focus help you move quickly toward the finish line, especially before an exam or a competition. Keep your pace, control distractions and do not let yourself be pulled in many directions.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may lose your way or burn out from studying too hard and too fast. Stop to adjust your pace, choose one priority and ask a guide for help if you feel stuck.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests progress through effort and discipline. You may reach a saving or investing goal if you hold to your plan. Control your spending and stay focused on long-term goals.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests uncontrolled spending or hasty financial decisions made out of a wish to win quickly. Slow down, review your plan and avoid risks that come from ego or competitive pressure.

mind.upright: For well-being, the Chariot encourages keeping up disciplined training or working toward a physical goal, with energy pointed forward. Exercise regularly and pay attention to rest. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are trying too hard or lacking motivation, which leads to stress. Adjust your pace, rest at the right time and do not let competition wear down your energy.

chariot.symbolism: The warrior stands in the chariot, wearing a crown with a star and armor carved with moon symbols, showing willpower that steers emotion with reason. Two sphinxes, one black and one white, pull the chariot without reins, hinting at self-driven will rather than force, and that two opposing forces must be led in harmony. The canopy of stars overhead connects with the sky and suggests the guidance of the spirit. The city gate and river behind him are the world left behind. The two moons on his shoulders stand for change. The card carries the number 7, the number of the journey, and is linked to the element of Water and the sign of the Crab, a symbol of protection.
chariot.miu: Vroom vroom! Miu is driving the chariot… well, the cardboard box. But the speed is truly terrifying.

strength.name: Strength
strength.meaning_upright: Strength is not about muscle but about the inner power of a steady heart. The card shows you can tame fear, anger or raw instinct with patience and gentleness instead of force. You are invited to face challenges with calm courage, trusting your own endurance and generosity. When you treat yourself and others with understanding, what once felt frightening slowly softens. This is a time to stay calm, persist and let compassion lead. True strength is knowing you are afraid and still stepping forward, and it is the ability to stay with an uncomfortable feeling without being swallowed by it.
strength.meaning_reversed: When Strength is reversed, you may doubt your own ability or feel your inner strength running low. Fear, irritability or instinct may be overriding reason, so you react instead of acting with intent. You may also be trying to look strong to hide how fragile you feel. The card reminds you not to blame yourself; begin by caring for your feelings and resting. Regain confidence through small steps, and speak to yourself in a gentle voice instead of a critical one. Being strong does not mean never being weak.

love.upright: In love, Strength suggests patience, generosity and trust. A relationship can overcome difficulties through gentleness and understanding. You show affection in a mature way, know how to listen, and do not use control to hold on to someone.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you feel insecure, jealous or quick to anger in matters of the heart. You may lack the confidence to open up, or on the other hand be holding yourself too tightly. Heal the fear within before expecting anything from the other person.

career.upright: In your career, this is the card of persistence and soft leadership. You get through pressure with calm and settle conflict with understanding. The challenge may be large, but your inner strength is enough to carry things through a hard phase.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you are losing confidence or burning out under pressure. You may be handling conflict in a hurry. Rest, look again at your own worth, and do not compare yourself with others.

study.upright: In study, patience and perseverance now matter more than talent. For a difficult subject, learn slowly, with confidence, and face the fear of failure by being gentle with yourself.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be losing confidence or feeling discouraged by a hard subject. Break the content into pieces, celebrate small progress and remind yourself that slow does not mean poor.

finance.upright: In finances, the card encourages calm and discipline in the face of change. Be patient with long-term plans and do not let fear or greed drive your decisions. Inner steadiness helps you handle money wisely.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns that financial decisions may be driven by fear or impulse. You may lack confidence in managing money. Learn more, consult someone with experience, and decide when your mind is calm.

mind.upright: For well-being, Strength emphasizes physical and mental endurance. Keep steady habits, treat your body gently and listen to your needs. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests your energy is running low, your spirits are easily shaken, or you are pushing through too hard. Rest, seek support from people close to you, and care for your feelings as you would care for your body.

strength.symbolism: A woman in white gently strokes the jaw of a lion, showing instinct tamed by love instead of violence. The infinity sign above her head echoes the Magician, recalling boundless will and spiritual power. The wreath of flowers around her waist and head stands for harmony with nature. The lion, a symbol of instinct and passion, bows obediently, showing that inner strength wins over raw strength. The white of her dress is purity, and the yellow sky carries a warm, optimistic energy. The distant mountains hint at the journey already traveled. The card carries the number 8 and is linked to the element of Fire, the sign of Leo and the Sun.
strength.miu: Miu once tamed a lion. Its name was Chubby, and it was the neighbor's cat. But it still counts!

hermit.name: The Hermit
hermit.meaning_upright: The Hermit invites you to step back from the noise and look for answers within. The card suggests a phase of self-reflection, when you need time alone to think about the meaning, goals and true path of your life. This is not loneliness but a conscious choice to listen to your inner voice. The lantern in the hermit's hand lights only the next few steps, which means you do not need to see the whole road to begin. Seek guidance from your intuition or from a teacher you trust. When you are quiet enough, the answers become clearer. Wisdom often blooms in stillness, and it is also when you can share that light with others.
hermit.meaning_reversed: When reversed, solitude can turn into isolation or avoidance. You may be withdrawing too much, avoiding others for fear of being hurt, or refusing to hear advice. It is also possible you are swept up in noise and are not making time for yourself. The card reminds you to find balance between independence and connection. Ask yourself whether you are lonely or simply still, and if you need to, open up to someone you trust. Do not let the search for yourself become an excuse to stay away from life.

love.upright: In love, the Hermit suggests a phase of getting to know yourself; you may need quiet before starting a new relationship. For those in a couple, it points to a need for personal space. Share this with your partner sincerely.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests distance, loneliness or a fear of closeness. You may be pulling back too much. Try opening up bit by bit and say what you need instead of staying silent.

career.upright: In your career, this is a good time for research, deep study and reorienting. Work that needs focus, independence or advising suits you. Take time to think about what you truly want before deciding on your next step.
career.reversed: Reversed, you may be working alone too much or unwilling to take feedback. Connect with colleagues, find a mentor and balance focus with collaboration.

study.upright: In study, this is a phase for self-study, deep research and finding a good teacher. Quiet time alone will help you understand a topic thoroughly rather than skimming many things.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be isolating yourself too much or avoiding asking for help. Step out and talk with others, because an outside view will help you get unstuck.

finance.upright: In finances, take time to review your situation carefully and set long-term goals. Cautious decisions based on research rather than outside noise will suit you. Living simply may also be a wise choice.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are avoiding looking squarely at your finances, or are too closed to ask for opinions. Seek trustworthy advice and face the numbers calmly.

mind.upright: For well-being, the Hermit encourages rest, meditation, quiet walks and time for your inner life. A purposeful stretch of solitude helps you recover. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests that prolonged loneliness or too much withdrawal may affect your mood. Keep in touch with people close to you, and if things feel heavy, do not hesitate to seek professional support.

hermit.symbolism: The hermit stands on a snow-covered mountaintop in a gray cloak, symbolizing separation from a noisy world in order to find the truth. The lantern in his hand holds a six-pointed star, the seal of Solomon, standing for knowledge and inner light that guides those who follow. The long staff is the support and authority of experience. The high peak suggests spiritual achievements reached, and the quiet gray background shows calm. He looks down, as if reflecting inward instead of looking out. The card carries the number 9, the number of a completed cycle, and is linked to the element of Earth and the sign of Virgo, a symbol of refinement and analysis.
hermit.miu: Some days Miu climbs into a box and does not come out. It is not sadness; Miu is just thinking about the universe.

wheel.name: Wheel of Fortune
wheel.meaning_upright: The Wheel of Fortune reminds you that life moves in cycles of rise and fall, and nothing stays the same forever. The card often signals a turning point, good fortune or a change outside your control. A sudden opportunity may be on its way, or a new phase about to open. What matters is that you welcome change with flexibility and trust in a larger flow. When the wheel turns, look for ways to move along with it instead of trying to stand still in one place. The card also reminds you that your actions plant seeds for the next turn. Be grateful in good times and patient in hard ones, because every stage is only a part of the journey.
wheel.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may feel that luck is against you, or that you are resisting a change that cannot be avoided. You may be repeating an old pattern because you have not yet drawn the lesson from it. The card also hints at temporary delays that make everything seem stuck. Do not rush to blame fate; look at which parts you can change. Accept what is outside your control and focus on what you can do. The wheel is still turning, and patience will help you get through this phase.

love.upright: In love, the card suggests a fated meeting or a turning point in a relationship. It could be an unexpected encounter, or a relationship moving into a new phase. Welcome change with trust and flexibility.
love.reversed: Reversed, it shows you repeating an old romantic pattern or meeting a temporary setback. Look back at the lessons of the past and be patient; do not push the relationship faster than its own pace.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals opportunity, a turning point or a change of position. Be ready to adapt and seize the moment. A new cycle may open, so prepare your skills to meet it.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests unexpected obstacles, delays or a feeling of being stuck in a work loop. Review your strategy, learn from earlier attempts and stay flexible.

study.upright: In study, there is a turning point or an unexpected opportunity, such as a scholarship, a change of program or a result that changes the picture. Be ready to adapt and take the chance when it appears.
study.reversed: Reversed, results may not be what you hoped, or your plans may be temporarily disrupted. This is a cycle, not a sentence; learn from it and prepare for the next round.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a change in fortune, which may be a new opportunity or fluctuation. Stay flexible, keep a reserve fund and do not depend entirely on luck. Decisions with a solid base are still the better choice.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of fluctuations or unexpected expenses. Be careful with risk, avoid relying on luck and review financial habits that have repeated many times.

mind.upright: For well-being, the Wheel suggests cycles of ups and downs and the importance of a steady rhythm of life. Adapt to changes in your body and keep stable habits. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests bad habits repeating or a disordered daily rhythm. Find the root cause and change in small steps rather than expecting instant change.

wheel.symbolism: The wheel at the center is inscribed with the letters TARO, which can be read as ROTA, TORA or ATOR, hinting at many layers of meaning about law and cycles. The four winged creatures in the corners, a man, a lion, a bull and an eagle, are the four evangelists and the four fixed signs of the zodiac, reading books like eternal observers. A snake descends on the left, Anubis rises on the right, and a sphinx sits on top holding a sword in balance, showing opposition and order. The alchemical symbols on the wheel speak of the transformation of matter. The blue clouds stand for the unseen world. The card carries the number 10 and is linked to the element of Fire and the planet Jupiter, the planet of good fortune.
wheel.miu: The wheel turns, Miu chases it… then gets dizzy. Lesson: sometimes just let it turn and sit back and watch.

justice.name: Justice
justice.meaning_upright: Justice is the card of truth, fairness and cause and effect. It reminds you that every action has consequences and that in the end balance is restored. You may be facing a decision that calls for objectivity, a legal matter, or a situation that requires you to see things honestly. Weigh matters with reason, listen to all sides and take responsibility for your choices. When you act with integrity, results tend to go in a fair direction. The card also encourages you to face the truth, even when it is not comfortable. True justice is not punishment but the restoring of order and harmony. Ask yourself: am I living in line with what I believe?
justice.meaning_reversed: When reversed, injustice or a lack of transparency may be happening around you. You may also be avoiding responsibility, making excuses or not looking squarely at the consequences of your actions. Bias, missing information or hasty judgment can all distort a decision. The card reminds you to check whether you are honest with yourself. Gather full information, correct mistakes when needed and look for a fair solution. If there is a legal dispute, consult a professional for proper guidance.

love.upright: In love, Justice suggests balance, honesty and responsible commitment. A relationship needs fairness between two people. Speak truthfully, listen, and make decisions based on mutual respect.
love.reversed: Reversed, it shows imbalance, a lack of honesty or unfairness in a relationship. One person may be avoiding responsibility. Talk frankly and acknowledge your own part in the problem.

career.upright: In your career, the card supports transparency, professional ethics and contract matters. You may receive deserved recognition. Read documents carefully, work with integrity and make objective decisions.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests unfairness at work or contracts that are not yet clear. Check your paperwork, record information and be careful with people who lack honesty. Own your share if there has been a mistake.

study.upright: In study, your effort will be fairly recognized, especially in exams and assessments. Study honestly, read the conditions and rules closely and prepare your paperwork for procedures.
study.reversed: Reversed, there may be errors, results not as you wished, or you may be taking shortcuts. Check the rules again, be honest with yourself and do not blame everything on circumstances.

finance.upright: In finances, Justice reminds you of balance between income and spending, and of tax, contract or legal matters. Spend responsibly, keep clear records and decide on the basis of full information.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial disputes or a lack of transparency. Read terms carefully, keep receipts and seek professional advice if there is a legal issue.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you to balance your lifestyle and to notice the cause and effect between habits and how your body feels. Adjust to find harmony between work and rest. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests long-standing imbalance or avoiding the consequences of your habits. Be honest with yourself and adjust step by step to regain your balance.

justice.symbolism: The figure sits on a throne wearing a crown, holding a sword upright in the right hand and a pair of scales in the left. The double-edged sword means that reason and fairness come with consequences, while the scales stand for weighing right and wrong. The purple curtain behind is the spiritual foundation, and the two pillars at the sides suggest standards. The red cloak is action, and the square crown shows order and logic. One shoe peeks out beneath the gown, as if to say that justice is always ready to step forward. The card carries the number 11 in the RWS system and is linked to the element of Air and the sign of Libra, the symbol of balance.
justice.miu: Sharing fish fairly: half for you, half for Miu, and the other half… for Miu too.

hanged.name: The Hanged Man
hanged.meaning_upright: The Hanged Man invites you to stop and look at everything in a different way. The card suggests a meaningful pause, when action is no longer effective and you need to let go in order to understand more. You may have to wait, or give something up in exchange for clarity. Instead of trying to control, let things unfold and observe from a new angle. The surrender here is not failure but trust. When you change how you see, an old problem may show up with another meaning. Use this stretch of time to reflect, because what you learn in stillness will take you further when action resumes.
hanged.meaning_reversed: When reversed, waiting can turn into delay or a stalemate. You may be resisting letting go, making sacrifices for nothing, or holding on to a situation that no longer fits. You may fear change and so get stuck in hesitation. The card asks: what am I waiting for, and am I locking myself in? It is time to choose a new perspective and act with intent. Do not let kindness toward others make you forget your own needs.

love.upright: In love, the card suggests a pause to understand each other better, or letting go of expectations. You may need patience for a while. Try seeing things from the other person's side and change your approach instead of forcing matters.
love.reversed: Reversed, it shows you stuck in a relationship, sacrificing too much or putting off a necessary decision. Say what you feel and set boundaries.

career.upright: In your career, a project may be put on hold or need reconsidering. Use the wait to learn, change your perspective and prepare. Sometimes letting go of an old goal opens the way to something better.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are stuck, delaying decisions or overworking without recognition. Review your goals and boldly change your approach.

study.upright: In study, progress may seem to slow, but this is a time to change your view and let knowledge soak in. A subject seen in a new way will become easier to understand.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be putting things off or stuck because you will not change how you study. Decide to let go of a method that is not working, and act.

finance.upright: In finances, this is a time to pause big decisions and reconsider how you see money. You may need to give up one expense to reach a long-term goal. Be patient and do not rush to act.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns that hesitation may make you miss opportunities, or that you are making unnecessary financial sacrifices. Review and make a decision with a plan.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card advises rest, relaxation and a new view on how you care for yourself. Activities such as meditation or gentle yoga may help. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are putting off self-care or enduring too much. Listen to your body and do not hesitate when you need support.

hanged.symbolism: A man hangs upside down from a T-shaped tree by one foot, with the other leg bent into the shape of a 4 and his hands tucked behind his back. His face is calm, with a halo around his head, showing that this is voluntary and not a punishment. The living tree stands for the world and for life, so this surrender is tied to a spiritual transformation. His blue tunic is reason, and his red trousers are passion turned upside down. The pale blue background suggests stillness. The card carries the number 12, which stands for a complete cycle, and is linked to the element of Water and the planet Neptune, the place of intuition and dissolving.
hanged.miu: Miu often hangs upside down off the arm of the chair. The upside-down world looks hilarious; have you tried it?

death.name: Death
death.meaning_upright: Death rarely speaks of death in the literal sense; it speaks of the ending that is needed for something new to begin. The card signals a phase closing, a habit, relationship or way of living that has reached its end. Even if it hurts, this is a natural transformation that helps you grow. When you dare to let go of what no longer serves you, space opens for new opportunities. Welcome change instead of clinging, and allow yourself to mourn what has passed. After the dark night comes dawn, and rebirth often arrives in unexpected ways. The card invites you to trust the cycles of life and to bravely step into the next chapter.
death.meaning_reversed: When Death is reversed, transformation slows because you resist or hold on. You may be clinging to something that is over, afraid of change, or living in the past. This stagnation leaves you feeling stuck, moving neither forward nor back. The card reminds you that endings cannot be avoided, but you can choose how to face them. Ask yourself what you are afraid of losing, and whether that fear is real. Allow yourself to let go little by little and you will feel lighter. Change comes sooner or later, and taking the initiative will help you pass through more gently.

love.upright: In love, Death suggests the end of a phase or a relationship, opening the way for new feelings or a more mature way of loving. Honor the past and allow yourself to heal.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are clinging to a relationship that has run dry, or finding it hard to let go of the past. Be honest about your feelings and let yourself move forward when you are ready.

career.upright: In your career, an old chapter may close: a project ending, a change of field or a restructuring. See it as a chance to renew. Learn new skills and be ready for a different direction.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you fear a career change or cling to work that no longer fits. Reassess and bravely make a new choice.

study.upright: In study, one phase ends to open another, such as graduating, changing majors or dropping an old way of learning. Do not regret it; see it as transformation.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be holding on to a path that no longer fits, or fearing change. Be brave in reassessing, and accept that changing direction is also progress.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a major change in how you manage things, perhaps cutting unnecessary expenses to start afresh. Accept adjustments and build a new, steadier foundation.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of holding on to old financial habits or fearing change. Take another look and make the necessary adjustments instead of putting them off.

mind.upright: For well-being, Death reminds you to end unhelpful habits and begin a new way of living. Transformation takes time, so be patient. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests difficulty giving up old habits or fear of changing your lifestyle. Break your goals into small parts and seek support to begin step by step.

death.symbolism: A skeleton in black armor rides a white horse and carries a flag with a five-petaled white rose, symbolizing purity and life triumphing over death. The white horse is the unstoppable force of change. A king lies beneath the horse's hooves, while a bishop, a maiden and a child stand before it, showing that death comes to everyone alike. In the distance, two towers and a sun rising between two pillars hint at hope and rebirth. The river flowing beside is the place of passage between two worlds. The card carries the number 13 and is linked to the element of Water and the sign of Scorpio, a symbol of deep transformation.
death.miu: Do not be afraid of this card! Cats have nine lives, and every change of life is a fresh start.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.meaning_upright: Temperance is the card of balance and harmony in every area of life. It invites you to find the middle ground between extremes, to blend reason and emotion, action and rest. This is a stage of patience, healing and moderation, when everything moves forward slowly but lastingly. You may be learning to reconcile contradictions or to find a rhythm of life that suits you better. Avoid excess, choose the middle way and let time do its part. An angel pouring water between two cups reminds you that creativity comes from combining things in harmony. When you are patient and trusting, you will find peace and a deeper meaning.
temperance.meaning_reversed: When reversed, imbalance shows up: you may be living to excess, rushing, or out of step among the parts of your life. Inner conflict, or conflict with others, may make it hard to find harmony. The card asks you to stop and see what is too much or too little. Adjust bit by bit; no sudden change is needed. Make time to rest, take care of yourself and learn to reconcile. When you find your own rhythm again, peace will return.

love.upright: In love, Temperance suggests a harmonious relationship with patience and understanding. The two of you know how to blend your differences. Communicate gently, share space and let feelings develop at their natural pace.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests being out of step or going to extremes in a relationship, such as giving too much or being impatient. Find a balance and talk to reconcile.

career.upright: In your career, the card supports cooperation, moderate work and steady progress. Be patient, keep a sustainable pace and combine different skills to achieve good results.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you working out of balance, overextended, or in conflict within a team. Adjust your workload and look for ways to reconcile.

study.upright: In study, balance between learning, rest and relationships is helping you be effective. Combine theory with practice and study steadily rather than cramming.
study.reversed: Reversed, your study schedule may be unbalanced: overloaded or too loose. Readjust your rhythm and avoid extremes; slow but steady beats cramming and burning out.

finance.upright: In finances, this is a time to manage moderately, balance income and spending and build a long-term base. Be patient with saving plans and avoid both overspending and being too tight-fisted.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests uncontrolled spending or an unbalanced budget. Review your plan, set limits and adjust gradually.

mind.upright: For well-being, Temperance encourages a balanced life: moderate eating, moderate exercise and enough rest. Healing takes patience. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests an unbalanced lifestyle, with too much work or too much play. Find a regular daily rhythm again and care for yourself gently.

temperance.symbolism: An angel with large wings stands with one foot in the water and one on land, pouring water between two cups, showing the blending of the subconscious and the conscious mind. The water flows on without running dry, suggesting continuous exchange. The triangle inside a square on the angel's chest stands for the union of spirit and matter. The path leading to a distant mountain with a glow is a journey toward enlightenment. Irises grow nearby, tied to Iris, goddess of the rainbow and messenger of the gods. The card carries the number 14 and is linked to the element of Fire and the sign of Sagittarius, but it carries the soothing energy of reconciliation.
temperance.miu: Mix milk with warm water, not hot, not cold. Miu calls that the art of moderation… and also a snack.

devil.name: The Devil
devil.meaning_upright: The Devil represents the chains you wear yourself, or are bound by. The card speaks of temptation, desire, habits that are hard to quit, or relationships built on dependence. Sometimes you are tied by limiting beliefs, fear or material things without realizing it. Notably, the chains in the card are quite loose, meaning you always have the ability to step out if you wish. The card invites you to look squarely at your own shadow and to admit your hidden wants and fears. When you see them clearly, their power shrinks. Ask yourself: what is controlling me, and what am I trading away for this comfort?
devil.meaning_reversed: When reversed, this can be a moment of recognition and release. You begin to see the bonds, bad habits or toxic relationships clearly, and you find the courage to leave. The process can be hard, but it brings freedom and a sense of agency. The card may also warn that you are still avoiding the truth or slipping into another temptation. Be patient with yourself, seek support when needed and take back control of your life step by step. You deserve to live freely and healthily.

love.upright: In love, the Devil suggests intense attraction that may come with dependence or jealousy. See whether the relationship is balanced and healthy, and do not let desire cloud respect.
love.reversed: Reversed, it shows you recognizing an unhealthy relationship and wanting out. This is the first step toward taking back your freedom. Seek support from someone you trust.

career.upright: In your career, the card warns of being tied to a job by money or status, or of a high-pressure environment. See whether you are trading away too much and find a way to reset your boundaries.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are looking for a way out of a toxic environment or taking back autonomy at work. Make a concrete plan and move one step at a time.

study.upright: In study, you may be caught up in bad habits such as scrolling, procrastinating or grade pressure. Recognize what is binding you and set clear limits on it.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are beginning to break free of habits that block your studies. Keep the momentum, seek support and do not blame yourself when you stumble.

finance.upright: In finances, the Devil warns of dependence on material things, impulsive spending or debt. Look squarely at your spending habits and at what you truly need.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are regaining control of your finances, breaking free of a spending habit or a burden. Keep up the discipline and seek professional advice if needed.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card points to habits that are hard to quit or to harmful dependence. Acknowledge them honestly and look for suitable support. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are on the way out of a bad habit. Recognize your effort, set small goals and ask loved ones or a professional to walk with you.

devil.symbolism: A half-goat, half-human creature with bat wings sits on a stone pedestal, with a raised hand and a torch above, the reverse of the Pope's blessing pose. The inverted pentagram on its forehead is an inversion of spiritual order. The two nude figures, man and woman, with slight horns and tails, are chained at the neck, but the chains are quite loose, showing they could take them off themselves. Their tails carry fire and grapes, like the Lovers but having fallen into temptation. The black background is obscurity, with no visible way out. The card carries the number 15 and is linked to the element of Earth and the sign of Capricorn, speaking of matter, bonds and the power of habit.
devil.miu: Miu's biggest temptation is a ball of yarn. I know it ends in a tangle, but… so much fun!

tower.name: The Tower
tower.meaning_upright: The Tower is the card of sudden upheavals that bring down whatever was built on shaky ground. Though it may be a shock, the event often leads to the truth coming out and the chance to rebuild more soundly. You may be facing a sudden change in work, a relationship or a belief. Feeling bewildered is natural, but this is also a moment of freedom from illusions. Stay calm, protect yourself and focus on the essentials. When the dust settles, you will see clearly what truly matters. From the rubble, you can build something more honest and lasting.
tower.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be avoiding a collapse that is needed, or living with the long aftermath of an old upheaval. You may also be clinging to what has already begun to wobble because you fear change. The card reminds you that putting off facing the truth only prolongs your unease. Be brave about looking at what is not right and adjust on your own initiative before it is too late. If you are recovering from a crisis, give yourself time and do not rush to rebuild. Healing has its own pace.

love.upright: In love, the Tower may signal a truth coming out or a sudden change in the relationship. Though difficult, this is a chance for the two of you to face each other honestly and rebuild or let go.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are avoiding a problem in the relationship or recovering from an emotional shock. Allow yourself to hurt and accept support when needed.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals upheaval such as restructuring, job loss or a project collapsing. Stay calm, protect your resources and see it as a chance to reorient.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you are avoiding necessary change or still feeling the aftershocks of a work crisis. Adjust proactively to reduce risk.

study.upright: In study, there may be a shock such as a low grade, a plan falling apart or discovering the wrong direction. Though unpleasant, it clears away shaky ground so you can rebuild more firmly.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be avoiding a truth you need to face, or recovering from a failure. Fix mistakes early instead of waiting for everything to collapse.

finance.upright: In finances, the Tower warns of sudden fluctuations. Keep a reserve fund and do not put all your hopes in one source. After the turbulence, rebuild a firmer foundation.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are avoiding a financial problem or recovering from a loss. Be patient, make a clear plan and seek professional advice.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you to listen to your body and mind when sudden stress appears. Make time to rest and look for support. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are bottling up stress or are slowly recovering. Keep taking care of yourself and do not ignore signs that need attention.

tower.symbolism: A tall tower on a mountaintop is struck by lightning, the crown thrown off and flames bursting from the windows, symbolizing the collapse of ego and of structures built on illusion. Two people fall from the tower, a symbol of lost control and of a letting go that had to happen. The lightning bolt is the sudden light of truth. The flame drops shaped like the letter Yod, twelve of them, recall the sacred hand and the Tree of Life. The dark sky sets off the moment of shock. The card carries the number 16 and is linked to the element of Fire and the planet Mars, carrying the energy of breaking down in order to renew.
tower.miu: The tower of cans Miu stacked all afternoon just came crashing down. But stacking it again the second time made it much prettier!

star.name: The Star
star.meaning_upright: The Star is the card of hope and healing after a storm. After upheaval, you enter a quiet phase where your soul is nourished and faith returns. The card invites you to open your heart to the universe, trust the future and allow yourself to recover. This is a time to reconnect with your dreams, your intuition and simple beauty. You do not need to hurry; just keep filling yourself with energy. Honesty, gentleness and gratitude will lead you. The bright star reminds you that even in the dark of night there is a light to guide you. Allow yourself to believe that good things are coming.
star.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may feel you have lost faith, are disappointed or lack motivation. After a hard stretch, it may be difficult to see hope and you may doubt the future. The card reminds you that the light is still there; you just have not seen it yet. Do small things that help restore your energy, such as resting, going out into nature or sharing with someone you trust. Do not compare yourself with others. Recovery takes time, and faith will return little by little when you treat yourself gently.

love.upright: In love, the Star brings healing, hope and honest connection. You may meet someone who makes you believe in love again, or your current relationship may deepen. Open your heart and let things unfold naturally.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are losing faith in love or feeling pessimistic. Give yourself time to heal and do not rush to conclusions. Loving yourself first is also a beautiful step.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages you to follow your passion, find inspiration and trust your long-term direction. New opportunities may appear gently. Work with sincerity and optimism.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you lack motivation or are disappointed with work. Find your purpose again, rest, and set small goals to regain inspiration.

study.upright: In study, this is a phase full of hope and inspiration. Your long-term goal becomes clearer; keep going and trust the process, even when results are not immediate.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may have lost confidence or find the future vague. Reset small, near goals and remind yourself why you began.

finance.upright: In finances, the Star suggests recovery and hope. Build a long-term plan and put your faith in sustainable steps. Stability comes gradually as you persist.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are worried or have lost faith about money. Start with small steps, set realistic goals and seek trustworthy advice.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents recovery, relaxation and recharging. Spend time in nature, drink enough water and look after your mind. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests drained energy or a lack of motivation to care for yourself. Rest, connect with loved ones and seek support if things feel heavy.

star.symbolism: A nude woman kneels by a pool, one foot on land and one in the water, pouring water from two jars, one into the pool and one onto the ground, showing nourishment of both the subconscious and the real world. Her nakedness is honesty and no longer being on the defensive. Eight stars in the sky, a large yellow one in the middle, speak of hope and guidance. The ibis on the tree behind is linked to Thoth, the god of wisdom. The lush landscape after a storm is a rebirth. The card carries the number 17 and is linked to the element of Air and the sign of Aquarius, a symbol of inspiration and humanity.
star.miu: Every night Miu counts the stars. Never finished once, but it is always more fun each time.

moon.name: The Moon
moon.meaning_upright: The Moon takes you into the hazy realm of the subconscious, where things are not as clear as they appear. The card suggests uncertainty, dreams and strong intuition, but also possible fear or illusion. You may be confused because information is incomplete or your feelings are too mixed. This is a time to go slowly, observe and not jump to conclusions. Listen to your intuition, but also tell the difference between intuition and anxiety. Keeping a dream journal or talking with someone you trust can help you understand more. When you dare to look at the hidden parts of yourself, the dark becomes less frightening. The road ahead is not yet bright, but the moonlight is enough for you to step one step at a time.
moon.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the fog begins to lift. You gradually understand what once confused you, or realize what you have been avoiding. This can be a release of anxiety and truth coming to light. However, the card can also warn that you are deceiving yourself or being deceived. Verify information and face your fear instead of suppressing it. When you name a fear, it often shrinks. Be patient and let clarity come bit by bit.

love.upright: In love, the Moon suggests deep but unclear feelings; something may be unsaid, or there may be insecurity. Trust your intuition but also ask directly; do not let imagination lead.
love.reversed: Reversed, it shows the truth gradually coming out, or you beginning to understand your own feelings. Communicate openly and settle old misunderstandings.

career.upright: In your career, information may be unclear or you may be undecided. This is not a time for quick decisions. Gather more data and trust your intuition, but check it against facts.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are getting more clarity at work or discovering something that was hidden. Handle the information carefully and avoid hasty reactions.

study.upright: In study, things may be unclear, with a tendency to worry or misunderstand. Do not decide while confused; ask again and verify information before you believe it.
study.reversed: Reversed, the fog is clearing and you are starting to see what you need to do. Deal with worry through concrete actions, like making a revision plan or asking someone experienced.

finance.upright: In finances, the Moon warns of uncertainty and unclear information. Avoid big decisions before you fully understand. Verify and ask someone you trust.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it shows you beginning to see your financial situation clearly or discovering hidden information. Review the details and adjust when needed.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card points to sleep, dreams and hidden feelings. Pay attention to your sleep rhythm, ease anxiety and look after your mind. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests anxiety easing or you understanding the source of your stress better. Keep seeking support and maintain habits that help you stay calm.

moon.symbolism: A full moon with a gentle face sits in the middle of the sky, casting light onto the path between two towers. A dog and a wolf, one tame and one wild, howl at the moon, symbolizing instinct and civilization. The crayfish crawling out of the water is new awareness rising from the subconscious. The winding path leading to distant mountains is a vague journey. Drops of light falling from the moon suggest an invisible influence on emotion. The two towers are the gate between two worlds. The card carries the number 18 and is linked to the element of Water and the sign of Pisces, the place of dreams, intuition and illusion.
moon.miu: Cats can see in the dark, and you have Miu. Just go slowly; Miu is holding the lantern.

sun.name: The Sun
sun.meaning_upright: The Sun is the card of joy, success and overflowing vitality. After hazy stretches, light returns and everything becomes clear and warm. The card speaks of genuine confidence, optimism and the feeling of being yourself. You may receive the fruits of your effort, a bright beginning or simple moments of happiness. Enjoy them, share your joy and be grateful for what you have. The Sun also reminds you to keep a child's innocence, to play and to be open. This is a time when things become transparent, and your positive energy can spread to those around you.
sun.meaning_reversed: When reversed, joy may be dimmed or incomplete. You may feel a little low on drive, or be so optimistic that you overlook reality. Success may arrive more slowly than you expected. The card is still a positive sign; you only need to adjust your perspective. Find joy in small things and avoid letting ego take over. If you feel a little sad, give yourself time to rest. The light is still there, and sometimes all you need is to step outside or connect with loved ones.

love.upright: In love, the Sun brings happiness, openness and sincerity. The relationship is bright and full of laughter and may move toward commitment. If you are single, you shine and attract others easily.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests joy that is not yet complete or expectations that are too high. Talk honestly and appreciate what you have instead of comparing.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals success, recognition and confidence. A project may go smoothly. Share your results, work in a positive spirit and keep growing.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows success arriving slowly or you overrating yourself. Be patient and realistic, and focus on the quality of your work.
