study.upright: In study, this is a very favorable card: good results, quick understanding and plenty of confidence. Enjoy the pleasure of learning and share it with friends, as they will benefit too.
study.reversed: Reversed, results may be slow or you may be overconfident. Even so, the positive energy remains; check your study method and do not overlook small details.

finance.upright: In finances, the Sun suggests stability, growth and peace of mind. The fruits of your effort may show up. Keep managing wisely and share your joy mindfully.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests being overly optimistic about money or results coming slower than expected. Keep a realistic plan and do not overspend.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents full energy, a positive mood and the benefits of sunshine and outdoor movement. Enjoy your vitality. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests slightly low energy or a lack of natural light. Go outside, move gently and rest enough to regain your vitality.

sun.symbolism: A large Sun with a face shines in a blue sky, with straight and wavy rays alternating, symbolizing energy and life. A nude child rides a white horse and raises a red banner, showing innocence, freedom and pure joy. The tall sunflowers behind, always turning to the sun, mean optimism and growth. The stone wall behind is a boundary already crossed. The white horse is pure strength that has been tamed. The card carries the number 19 and is linked to the element of Fire and the Sun, the source of all life.
sun.miu: Sunbathing is Miu's profession! You should soak up a bit of sun today too.

judgement.name: Judgement
judgement.meaning_upright: Judgement is a call to awaken, when you look back on your journey and welcome a phase of rebirth. The card invites you to evaluate yourself honestly, forgive the past and listen to the inner call that leads you to your true purpose. You may be at a turning point where you understand what you have learned and are ready to step into a new chapter. Forgive yourself and others, because that letting go sets you free. This is the time to answer your own calling and dare to live in line with what you believe. When you awaken to the truth, you can make clear decisions and move forward with confidence.
judgement.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be ignoring your inner call or judging yourself too harshly. Regret about the past or doubt makes you hesitate at the turning point. The card reminds you to face the lesson instead of avoiding it. Forgiving yourself does not mean ignoring mistakes; it means allowing yourself to move on. Listen to what truly wants to be said, and do not let other people's judgments drown out your voice.

love.upright: In love, Judgement suggests forgiveness, a fresh start, or understanding what you truly want. The relationship may enter a new phase after both of you look back. Be honest and receptive.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are holding on to old faults or blaming yourself. Let go of judgment and talk openly to heal, or to close the chapter in peace.

career.upright: In your career, this is a time to reassess and answer the call of your professional purpose. You may receive recognition or a chance to change direction. Be confident and act.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you hesitating over a career change or criticizing yourself too much. Look back at your achievements fairly and decide based on what you truly want.

study.upright: In study, this is a time to reassess your journey and make an important decision, such as a decisive exam or admissions result. Look back honestly and then act.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be too hard on yourself or putting off a decision you need to make. Learn from old mistakes instead of blaming yourself, and dare to move on.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests reviewing your situation, drawing lessons and making a new plan. Look squarely at the numbers, learn from the past and make conscious decisions.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are avoiding reviewing your finances or regretting an old decision. Forgive yourself and begin planning from the present.

mind.upright: For well-being, Judgement encourages you to look back at your habits and resolve to change. A fresh start is possible. Treat yourself gently. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are criticizing yourself or putting off change. Start with small steps and ask someone to accompany you so you can keep going.

judgement.symbolism: The angel Gabriel blows a trumpet from the clouds, with a cross flag on the horn, waking people who rise up from coffins set on the sea. They spread their arms to receive it, a man, a woman and a child, symbolizing the awakening of the whole person. The snowy mountains in the distance are purification and trials that have passed. The sea below is the subconscious, where memories rise up. The gray color of the risen figures shows they stand between death and new life. The card carries the number 20 and is linked to the element of Fire and the planet Pluto, the planet of rebirth.
judgement.miu: A trumpet sounds… oh, that is the sound of a pâté can being opened. Miu awakens instantly!

world.name: The World
world.meaning_upright: The World is the card of completion and wholeness. You have come through a long journey, received its lessons and achieved something important. This is a moment to celebrate, to acknowledge what you have accomplished and to feel in harmony with the world around you. The card also signals a cycle closing and a new door about to open. You may be free to travel, explore or broaden your horizons. Be grateful for what you have been through and enjoy the feeling of being complete. When a chapter ends, you carry its wisdom into the next. This is a time when you see yourself as part of a larger picture.
world.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be close to the finish line but not quite done, or feel that a piece is missing. You may be delaying an ending because you fear stepping into a new phase. The card reminds you to see which tasks are still unfinished and to complete them calmly. Do not rush, but do not stop for too long either. Appreciate what you have achieved and let yourself move forward. Wholeness does not require everything to be perfect, only that you are ready to close a chapter consciously.

love.upright: In love, the World suggests completeness, harmony and lasting commitment. A relationship reaches an important milestone, or you feel fulfilled beside the person you love. Treasure it and look toward a new chapter together.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a feeling of incompleteness or a missing piece in your feelings. Talk about what is missing and complete it patiently.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals success, a project finished, or an opportunity to expand, possibly internationally. Acknowledge your results and prepare for the next stage of growth.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a project not yet finished or you putting off the last step. Review what is still pending and complete it with patience.

study.upright: In study, you are completing an important stage, such as graduating, finishing a course or reaching a long-term goal. Acknowledge your results and think about the next stage.
study.reversed: Reversed, there is a little more to do before it is done, or you are missing the final step. Review what remains, finish it, and then move on to something new.

finance.upright: In finances, the World suggests stability, reaching your goals and being satisfied with the results. Keep managing well and set new goals for the next cycle.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a financial goal that is almost reached but not finished. Persist, avoid slackening at the final stage and review your plan.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents balance and harmony between body and mind. Keep up good habits and enjoy the feeling of wholeness. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are close to a health goal but need a little more effort. Be patient, complete your habits and do not give up at the last step.

world.symbolism: A dancer in a flowing purple sash steps through the air, holding two wands, in the middle of an oval laurel wreath, symbolizing the completion and harmony of the universe. The half-covering sash shows that truth still has depth. The four creatures in the corners, a man, an eagle, a bull and a lion, are the four elements and the four fixed signs of the zodiac, as in the Wheel of Fortune, but now complete. The laurel wreath is victory and the cycle. The card carries the number 21, ending the journey of the Major Arcana, and is linked to the element of Earth and the planet Saturn, representing structure and completion.
world.miu: Miu just ran a lap around the world… well, around the living room. But the finish-line feeling is exactly the same!

wands-ace.name: Ace of Wands
wands-ace.meaning_upright: The Ace of Wands is the first spark of an idea, a passion or a beginning full of energy. The hand from the cloud offers you a sprouting wand, like a message that the potential is already there, waiting for you to take it. You may feel inspired, wanting to start a new project, follow an interest or commit to an exciting direction. This is a time to act on enthusiasm, because your inner vitality is rising. Seize the moment, but also prepare to nurture the spark with planning and perseverance. What matters is that you dare to begin, since every great fire starts as a small ember.
wands-ace.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the spark may weaken or be blocked. You may have a good idea but lack the drive to act, or be held back by fear of failure. It is also possible that you start too many things and cannot keep them going. The card asks you to find out why you lost your enthusiasm: tiredness, lack of a goal or lack of confidence. Rest, reconnect with what excites you and begin with a very small step. The flame has not gone out; it only needs shelter from the wind and a gentle breath.

love.upright: In love, the Ace of Wands suggests new passion, strong attraction or the start of an energetic relationship. For those in a couple, it is a spark that renews the feelings. Take the initiative and show sincere enthusiasm.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests passion cooling or hesitation about starting a new relationship. You may fear rejection. Slow down and look into what you really want.

career.upright: In your career, this is a new opportunity, a breakthrough idea or a promising project. Act quickly but with direction, and use inspiration to kick off what you care about.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows an idea not yet carried out or a lack of motivation to work. Define a clear goal and break it into pieces to make starting easier.

study.upright: In study, a new source of inspiration or a new idea has just flared up. Get started right away on the topic, subject or project you are excited about.
study.reversed: Reversed, enthusiasm has not turned into action or was put out early. Pick one small thing to begin today instead of waiting for enough motivation.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a new opportunity such as a source of income, a project or a small business idea. Experiment with an open mind but stay cautious, and only invest what you could accept losing.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of a late opportunity or an idea without a plan. Check feasibility before putting in capital and do not rush because of passing excitement.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents vitality and the drive to begin a new habit such as exercise. Start gently and keep it steady. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests low energy or difficulty beginning a healthy habit. Set small goals, rest enough and find someone to go along with you.

wands-ace.symbolism: A hand emerges from a cloud holding a wand that is sprouting green leaves, symbolizing new life and potential not yet formed. The falling leaves look like sparks, suggesting a source of creative energy. The landscape below, with a river, mountains and a distant castle, speaks of the journey and ambition ahead. The cloud is the unseen source of inspiration. The wand is the symbol of the element of Fire, linked to passion, will and action. The Aces of the deck always carry the meaning of seeds, and the Ace of Wands is the seed of passion and creativity.
wands-ace.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: begin.

wands-2.name: Two of Wands
wands-2.meaning_upright: The Two of Wands is the card of a person standing atop a castle, looking out at the world and planning the next step. You have a little achievement already, but your vision is now wider. This is the time to consider whether to stay in your comfort zone or step out to explore. The card encourages you to think strategically, prepare and believe in your ability. A decision need not be rushed, but do not let safety make you miss an opportunity. Set long-term goals and define your first steps. When you know clearly what you want, the world ahead will open up and you will have the courage to go on.
wands-2.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may hesitate, fear risk or lack a concrete plan. You may be settling into your comfort zone even though you know you want more. You may also be planning too long without acting. The card asks: what fear is holding me back? Gather information, set a gentle deadline and take the first small step. Sometimes a vision needs time to ripen, but do not let it remain only a dream.

love.upright: In love, the Two of Wands suggests weighing your shared direction, or widening your own world. Share plans for the future and see whether the two of you are looking the same way.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests hesitation or different goals. Say plainly what you want and do not let fear of change hold you back.

career.upright: In your career, this is a phase of planning to expand, weighing new opportunities or a faraway project. Think strategically, study the market and prepare your next step.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a lack of planning or a reluctance to take risks. Build a clear roadmap and begin with small experiments before going the long way.

study.upright: In study, you are weighing your next direction, such as a field, a school or a program. Make a long-term plan and choose a direction with a far-sighted view.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be reluctant to leave your comfort zone, or your plan is still vague. Find concrete information to ease your worry and dare to decide.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests long-term planning, weighing investment or expansion. Research carefully, diversify and set specific goals.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of a lack of planning or hasty financial decisions. Review again and do not give up out of fear of change.

mind.upright: For well-being, set a long-term physical goal and make a realistic plan. A clear vision helps maintain motivation. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of a self-care plan or reluctance to change your lifestyle. Set small goals and start step by step.

wands-2.symbolism: A man stands on the castle wall, holding in his left hand a small globe that stands for the world and in his right a wand, while the other wand is fixed to the wall. He looks out at the sea and the horizon, showing a longing to explore. His red robe and orange cap carry the energy of Fire. The red roses and white lilies in the design recall the union of passion and wisdom. The landscape behind, with fields and mountains, is what has been achieved. The card is linked to the sign of Aries and the planet Mars, stressing initiative and determination.
wands-2.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: make a plan.

wands-3.name: Three of Wands
wands-3.meaning_upright: The Three of Wands shows that you have begun your journey and are now watching your plans sail out to sea. The figure on the cliff watches the ships, as if waiting for the fruits to come home. The card suggests expansion, opportunities arriving from afar and progress after your first efforts. You may be seeing the first signs of results, or preparing to expand into a new area. Be patient, trust your plan and keep a long view. This is also a time to cooperate, find partners and connect more widely. Once you have laid the foundation, what remains is to let things grow and to be ready to adapt.
wands-3.meaning_reversed: When reversed, plans may be slow or meet unexpected obstacles. You may be disappointed that results are not what you expected, or unprepared for a phase of expansion. Your vision may also not be clear enough. The card asks you to reassess your strategy, find the cause of the delay and adjust. Do not rush to give up; sometimes all you need is patience or a different approach. Focus on what you can control.

love.upright: In love, the Three of Wands suggests a long-distance relationship, or slow but promising progress. Keep faith, communicate regularly and look toward the future together.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests distance, delay or disappointment in a relationship. Talk clearly and be patient with each other's pace.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals expansion, international cooperation or a project beginning to bear results. Use your network and look further ahead.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a slow project or a lack of preparation. Review your plan, look for support and adjust your strategy.

study.upright: In study, your early efforts are bringing results and chances to expand, such as an international exchange or a broader learning environment. Look ahead and prepare the next step.
study.reversed: Reversed, plans are delayed or results are not as expected. Be patient, check your preparation steps again and do not give up early.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests gradual growth and opportunities from afar. Be patient, diversify and prepare for a phase of expansion.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of slow investment returns or a plan with little preparation. Check the risks and do not expect quick profit.

mind.upright: For well-being, keep steady habits and trust the long-term process. Small efforts are adding up. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests slow progress or a lack of motivation to keep going. Adjust your goals, note small gains and do not be discouraged.

wands-3.symbolism: A figure stands on a cliff looking out to sea, with his back to the viewer, beside three wands planted in the ground, one of which he holds. The ships on the sea symbolize plans that have been sent out and are waiting to return. The warm yellow sky suggests hope. The red cloak and the far-looking gaze speak of vision and ambition. The distant mountain is a bigger goal. The card is linked to the sign of Aries, the element of Fire and the number 3, the number of expansion.
wands-3.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: expand.

wands-4.name: Four of Wands
wands-4.meaning_upright: The Four of Wands is the card of joy and of celebrating a milestone. Four wands draped with flowers form a welcoming gate, and beneath it people dance, a symbol of harmony and shared results. You may be reaching an achievement, moving into a new home, marking an anniversary or gathering with loved ones. The card reminds you to stop and enjoy what you have built. Stability and a sense of community are the base for the next stage. Share your joy, appreciate those who walk with you and let yourself feel safe. Celebration is also a way of acknowledging the journey you have made.
wands-4.meaning_reversed: When reversed, harmony may be wobbling or a celebration is postponed. You may feel you do not yet belong, or there may be tension in the family or the group. You may also be in a transition where the sense of stability is not yet complete. The card reminds you to talk openly and rebuild the shared foundation. Do not feel pressure to be perfect; find joy in small moments and connect sincerely with the people around you.

love.upright: In love, the Four of Wands suggests closeness, a wedding, an engagement or a stable, joyful relationship. Cherish shared moments and share your happiness with loved ones.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests disagreement about commitment or family tension. Talk frankly and build trust step by step.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals recognized achievement, a good collaborative environment or a completed project. Celebrate with your team and strengthen team spirit.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows discord in the team or results not yet recognized. Improve communication and clarify roles.

study.upright: In study, a milestone worth celebrating, such as finishing a subject, defending a thesis or being accepted to a class. Celebrate with friends and with the people who helped you.
study.reversed: Reversed, the learning environment may lack cohesion, or you worry about stability. Build a study group that supports each other.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests stability, results from effort and the possibility of investing in a home or family. Enjoy it, but keep moderation.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial disagreement in the family or overspending on parties. Make a clear budget.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages joy, social connection and rest after a period of effort. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from relationships or from your living environment. Find a peaceful space and someone you trust to share with.

wands-4.symbolism: Four wands decorated with garlands form a welcoming canopy, with a castle behind, a place of safety and prosperity. Two people raise bouquets and dance in joy. The crowd in the distance shows a community sharing in the happiness. The yellow sky and green background suggest abundance. The card is tied to the number 4, the number of a solid foundation, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to the sign of Aries, carrying a spirit of victory and celebration.
wands-4.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: celebrate.

wands-5.name: Five of Wands
wands-5.meaning_upright: The Five of Wands shows five people with staves who seem to be sparring, each with a different idea, creating chaos. The card speaks of competition, differences of opinion or a battle of wits. Though it may bring tension, this conflict is also a chance to sharpen ideas and assert yourself. See it as a constructive challenge rather than a war. You need to stay calm, listen and tell healthy debate from aggression. Sometimes friction helps everyone find a new solution. Choose a fight worth having and know when to cooperate.
wands-5.meaning_reversed: When reversed, conflict may calm down and lead to reconciliation, or you may be avoiding a confrontation that is needed. Competition may also become covert and hard to see. Prolonged tension can wear you out. The card reminds you to settle things through dialogue instead of fighting. If you can, compromise and find common ground. Do not avoid issues that need discussing forever, because they will pile up.

love.upright: In love, the Five of Wands suggests arguments or differences that need to be resolved. It can also be competition between suitors. Keep respect, state your views clearly and listen.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests making up after an argument or avoiding an emotional issue. Talk gently and seek a compromise.

career.upright: In your career, the card shows a competitive environment, many conflicting opinions or a project that needs brainstorming. Use the diversity to create and to show your ability.
career.reversed: Reversed, it suggests hidden competition or avoiding conflict at work. Clarify roles and look for cooperation instead of confrontation.

study.upright: In study, competition, debate or pressure about grades is high. See it as a chance to build resilience and keep a healthy spirit with your classmates.
study.reversed: Reversed, conflict in a group may settle down, or you are avoiding competition. Look for ways to cooperate instead of opposing.

finance.upright: In finances, the card warns of competition or disagreement about money. Negotiate clearly and avoid unnecessary disputes.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a dispute being resolved or a need to compromise. Be transparent and consider a fair agreement.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card points to stress and pent-up energy. Exercise, release stress in healthy ways and rest. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests prolonged stress or exhaustion from conflict. Find ways to relax and set clear boundaries.

wands-5.symbolism: Five young men in different colorful outfits hold staves and point them at one another on dry grass. No one has the upper hand, showing that the struggle is more chaotic than a true confrontation. The different colors stand for a diversity of views. The clear blue sky shows that this conflict is not malicious. The card is tied to the number 5, the number of challenge and change, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to Saturn in Leo, the place of competition and self-assertion.
wands-5.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: conflict.

wands-6.name: Six of Wands
wands-6.meaning_upright: The Six of Wands is the card of victory and recognition. The rider with a laurel wreath moving through a cheering crowd is the image of results after effort. You may be receiving praise, reaching a goal or overcoming a challenge. Allow yourself to enjoy well-earned pride and thank the people who walked with you. The card strengthens your confidence and suggests you can lead others by example. Still, stay humble, because success also needs to be sustained. This is a time to keep the momentum going and to share the joy.
wands-6.meaning_reversed: When reversed, success may be slow or not recognized as you hoped. You may feel disappointed, insecure or afraid you do not deserve it. Your ego may also be taking over, leaving you dependent on praise. The card reminds you to find value from within, not only through outside recognition. Notice your own progress and keep making the effort. True success is feeling satisfied with the journey.

love.upright: In love, the Six of Wands suggests attractive confidence, a relationship others admire or a milestone worth celebrating. Be proud of yourself and share the joy with your partner.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of confidence or an ego that creates distance. Be sincere, avoid comparing and respect the other person.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals promotion, a finished project or recognition. Credit your teammates and use this momentum to go further.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows results not yet recognized or pressure to prove yourself. Assess yourself objectively and persevere.

study.upright: In study, effort is recognized through good grades, awards or praise. Enjoy the results and use this confidence for the next step.
study.reversed: Reversed, results may not be acknowledged, or you compare yourself with others. Judge yourself by your own progress.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests success from effort, such as higher income or a goal reached. Keep up discipline and share the results sensibly.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of spending to show off or results not as expected. Be realistic and focus on the foundation.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents confidence and recovery. Acknowledge progress and keep good habits. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of motivation or comparing yourself with others. Focus on personal progress rather than other people's expectations.

wands-6.symbolism: A rider on a white horse wears a laurel wreath and holds a wand with a victory wreath attached, passing through a crowd of cheering people holding staves. The white horse and the green tunic suggest pure strength and life. The red cloak stresses will and pride. The laurel wreath is the traditional symbol of victory. The crowd are supporters, a reminder that success also depends on community. The card is tied to the number 6, the number of harmony, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to Jupiter in Leo.
wands-6.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: victory.

wands-7.name: Seven of Wands
wands-7.meaning_upright: The Seven of Wands is the figure on the high hill, defending a position against many who are advancing. The card speaks of holding your ground and protecting what you believe in or have built. You may be facing competition, criticism or pressure, but you have the advantage and are able to stand firm. Be confident, steadfast and use your courage. It is also a reminder to choose what is worth defending and not spend your strength on unnecessary battles. When you believe in your own worth, you can get through the challenge.
wands-7.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may feel exhausted from constantly defending, or want to give in because of too much pressure. You may also be overreacting to small criticisms. The card asks you to look again at what you are protecting and whether it is necessary. Rest, find support and set healthy boundaries. Sometimes letting go of a fight is the wise way to keep your energy.

love.upright: In love, the Seven of Wands suggests you are protecting a relationship or standing up for what you believe. Keep clear boundaries, but do not turn your partner into an opponent.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are tired of having to prove something, or too defensive. Open up, communicate and allow yourself to be supported.

career.upright: In your career, the card advises you to hold your position and protect your results. Competition may rise, but you have the advantage. Be confident and well prepared.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows too much pressure or a feeling of being overwhelmed. Prioritize important tasks, ask for support and do not hesitate to rest.

study.upright: In study, you must defend your view or position under pressure. Stay steady, prepare solid arguments and do not lose heart.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may feel overloaded or want to quit. Choose your priorities and ask for support instead of trying to carry everything alone.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests protecting your resources and keeping discipline in the face of competition. Be careful and stand firm with your plan.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial pressure or giving in too much. Review your priorities and seek trustworthy advice.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you to conserve energy, set boundaries with pressure and look after yourself. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests exhaustion from stress. Rest, lighten your load and find someone to support you.

wands-7.symbolism: A figure stands at the top of a hill holding a wand raised in defense, while six wands from below reach up to attack. He wears two different shoes, hinting at haste and surprise yet still resolute. The high position shows advantage. The open green background reminds us that there is room to choose. The card is tied to the number 7, the number of challenge, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to Mars in Leo, showing courage in defense.
wands-7.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: defend.

wands-8.name: Eight of Wands
wands-8.meaning_upright: The Eight of Wands is the card of speed and fast movement. Eight wands fly through a peaceful sky toward their destination, showing events moving ahead strongly. You may receive news, an opportunity or a change that arrives quickly. Seize the momentum, act decisively and keep communication flowing. The card also suggests trips or plans being pushed forward. When everything is favorable, what matters is keeping a clear direction so speed does not turn into chaos. Trust the flow and be ready to adapt.
wands-8.meaning_reversed: When reversed, things may slow down, be delayed or move too hastily and chaotically. You may miss an opportunity for lack of preparation, or be overwhelmed by too many tasks. The card reminds you to slow down and check the details. Set priorities and communicate clearly. A delay is not always bad; it may help you rearrange.

love.upright: In love, the Eight of Wands suggests fast progress, frequent messages or an unexpected meeting. Keep communication open and take initiative, but do not rush too much.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests misunderstanding from slow communication or uneven pacing. State your wishes clearly and respect each other's speed.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a project moving quickly, an unexpected opportunity and smooth communication. Act and use the momentum.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows delay, overload or a lack of coordination. Arrange your priorities and make sure information is clear.

study.upright: In study, things move fast: messages, results, procedures or exam schedules arrive in a rush. Use this momentum and act efficiently.
study.reversed: Reversed, there may be delays, mixed-up schedules or inaccurate information. Check deadlines again and keep clear contact.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests quick change or a smooth transaction. Act with consideration and avoid deciding too hastily.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of hasty decisions or delayed transactions. Check information and do not overlook details.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card suggests lively energy and quick progress. Make use of it, but do not overdo it. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests overload or a rushed pace of life. Slow down and get enough rest.

wands-8.symbolism: Eight wands fly diagonally through the air with no people, and beneath them is a peaceful scene of a river and green hills. The parallel direction of flight shows a clear goal and unified energy. The blue sky is openness and freedom. The absence of people stresses that events are unfolding on their own momentum. The card is tied to the number 8, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to Mercury in Sagittarius, relating to information and movement.
wands-8.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: speed.

wands-9.name: Nine of Wands
wands-9.meaning_upright: The Nine of Wands shows a bandaged, tired figure who still stands firm before a fence of wands. You have come through many challenges and are close to the finish line, even if you feel exhausted. The card honors perseverance and the ability to get back up after setbacks. Spend a little last strength, because you have come too far to give up. At the same time, recognize your limits and rest at the right time. The experience you have gathered makes you more alert, but do not let it turn into suspicion of everything. You are stronger than you think.
wands-9.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be so exhausted you want to quit, or so defensive that you doubt everything. You may also be stubbornly enduring without asking for help. The card asks you to reassess: is it worth continuing, and what support do you need? Do not let the past make you lose faith in the future. Rest, open up and allow yourself to accept help.

love.upright: In love, the Nine of Wands suggests caution after old hurts, or a relationship getting through a trial. Open your heart little by little and accept support.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are too defensive and find it hard to trust others. Give yourself a chance to heal and speak honestly about your fears.

career.upright: In your career, the card shows you are nearly done though tired. Persist, but remember to rest and ask for support.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows exhaustion or a wish to quit. Review your workload and put your health first.

study.upright: In study, you are close to the finish though quite tired. Persist a little longer, but remember to rest to keep your strength.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are exhausted or want to give up just before the end. Lighten the load, put your health first and come back at a more sustainable pace.

finance.upright: In finances, the card advises perseverance and caution after difficulties. Keep a reserve fund and avoid unnecessary risk.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial exhaustion or being too defensive. Ask for advice and make a recovery plan.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you that you have endurance but need to recover. Sleep enough, rest and reduce stress. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests serious exhaustion or prolonged stress. Rest and seek support in time.

wands-9.symbolism: A man with a bandage on his head leans on a wand, with eight wands arranged behind him like a fence. The wary glance to the side shows that he is always ready. The wound is a trace of past battles. The ninth wand is what he leans on, showing endurance. The grayish-yellow background gives the feeling of being tired but not yet fallen. The card is tied to the number 9, the number of near completion, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to the Moon in Sagittarius.
wands-9.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: endurance.

wands-10.name: Ten of Wands
wands-10.meaning_upright: The Ten of Wands is the image of a person carrying a heavy bundle of wands toward the village. The card speaks of burden and responsibility, sometimes taken on by yourself too much. You may be busy and stressed but close to your goal. Ask yourself whether these burdens are really yours, and whether they can be shared or handed off. Your effort deserves recognition, but do not trade away your health and joy. When you focus on the destination and ask for help when you need it, you will get through this heavy phase.
wands-10.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be putting down some of the load, learning to delegate, or finally feeling so overloaded that you cannot go on. You may also be refusing a necessary responsibility. The card asks you to reassess your priorities, find what truly matters and let go of what you do not need. Do not hesitate to ask for help. Resting is not failure.

love.upright: In love, the Ten of Wands suggests you are carrying too much in the relationship. Share responsibilities and say what you need.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are learning to put some down, or avoiding commitment because of overload. Talk and divide things fairly.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a large workload and heavy responsibility. Divide it, prioritize and ask for support to reach your goal.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows exhaustion or that you are handing off some work. Reassess the workload and protect your health.

study.upright: In study, you are taking on too many subjects, projects or responsibilities. Break things down, say no to what is unnecessary and ask for support.
study.reversed: Reversed, you have put down some of the load or are exhausted from carrying too much. Redistribute and do not try to make everything perfect.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a heavy burden of financial responsibility. Make a clear plan and look for ways to reduce the pressure.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests lightening the load or collapsing under overload. Rearrange your priorities and ask for advice.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card warns of physical and mental stress from overwork. Rest and share the load. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are learning to reduce your load. Keep caring for yourself and do not take on extra work you do not need.

wands-10.symbolism: A man stoops under ten heavy wands, walking toward a house in the distance. He has his back turned and cannot see the way, like someone so absorbed in work that he forgets to look around. The village in the distance is a destination close at hand. The orange-brown of his clothing is the color of toil. The card is tied to the number 10, the number of completion but also of weight, belongs to the element of Fire and is linked to Saturn in Sagittarius.
wands-10.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: the burden.

wands-page.name: Page of Wands
wands-page.meaning_upright: The Page of Wands is a young person full of enthusiasm, curiosity and readiness to try something new. The card suggests news or an inspiring idea, a chance to learn or to explore a passion. You are in an early stage, with plenty of energy but still in need of direction. Be open, cheerful and unafraid of making mistakes. This is the time to try many fields, connect and let curiosity lead. Keep your enthusiasm and learn from every experience. When you allow yourself to play and create, you will find what truly excites you.
wands-page.meaning_reversed: When reversed, enthusiasm may lack direction or fade quickly. You may be impulsive, starting many things without finishing. You may also get news you did not hope for or feel short of inspiration. The card reminds you to focus, be patient and listen to advice. Choose one goal and build perseverance.

love.upright: In love, the Page of Wands suggests cheerful flirting, new passion or someone with youthful energy. Enjoy the discovery and open communication.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of seriousness or impulsiveness. Be clear about your intentions and do not promise what you are not sure you can do.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a chance to learn, a creative project or good news. Experiment, find a mentor and keep a positive spirit.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a lack of direction or procrastination. Set concrete goals and keep your discipline.

study.upright: In study, a new idea, news or learning opportunity is arriving. Keep your excitement, try several directions and learn from those who came before.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may lack patience or drop things halfway. Choose one goal and follow it until you get a first result.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a small opportunity or a new idea. Experiment with small capital and learn as you go.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of impulsive spending or ideas without a plan. Research before you act.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages fun movement and trying a new activity. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests impatience in your habits. Choose an activity you truly enjoy so you can keep it up.

wands-page.symbolism: A young person in a yellow tunic patterned with fire salamanders stands in the desert, looking up at a wand that is sprouting. The desert scene stresses a beginning from a dry place, meaning potential is sprouting. The pyramids in the distance are challenge and ancient knowledge. The wand recalls the Ace of Wands, a spark turning into action. The hat with a red feather shows enthusiasm. The card belongs to the element of Earth within the suit of Fire, representing learning and discovery.
wands-page.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: explore.

wands-knight.name: Knight of Wands
wands-knight.meaning_upright: The Knight of Wands is a knight galloping at full speed, full of enthusiasm and ambition. The card suggests decisive action, adventure and pursuing a passion with strong vitality. You may want to dive into a project, a trip or a big change. This energy is magnetic and inspiring, but it needs direction so it does not burn out fast. Use your boldness, keep your confidence and learn to share your enthusiasm. What matters is knowing where you are running to, so that you are not merely running for the love of running.
wands-knight.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the energy can become hasty, hot-tempered or impatient. You may start many things without finishing them, or act regardless of consequences. You may also be delayed and disappointed. The card reminds you to control your speed, make plans and listen. Focus your enthusiasm in one clear direction.

love.upright: In love, the Knight of Wands suggests a captivating, enthusiastic person who may lack stability. Enjoy the passion while watching how lasting the commitment is.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of commitment or a hot temper. State your expectations clearly and avoid impulsive decisions.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals quick action, a risky opportunity or a change of path. Use the energy, but with a plan.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows haste, unfinished projects or impatience. Slow down and finish things one at a time.

study.upright: In study, you learn with lots of energy and want to move fast. Use this spirit but watch quality, and do not skip the foundations.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be rushing, unfocused or dropping things halfway. Slow down, make a plan and keep a steady pace.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a bold decision. Weigh the risk and do not bet too much.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of recklessness or impulsive spending. Check carefully before acting.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents abundant energy. Exercise with guidance and avoid overdoing it. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests exhaustion from doing too much. Adjust your pace and rest.

wands-knight.symbolism: The knight wears golden armor with a fire salamander motif, riding a horse with a raised front leg and holding a sprouting wand. The galloping horse shows fast action. The golden-orange cloak and red plume carry strong energy. The desert behind is like that of the Page of Wands, but now he is on the move. The card belongs to the element of Fire within the suit of Fire, representing decisiveness.
wands-knight.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: take action.

wands-queen.name: Queen of Wands
wands-queen.meaning_upright: The Queen of Wands is a radiant, confident, magnetic woman. The card suggests enthusiasm, independence and the ability to inspire. You may be shining, leading others or living true to who you are. Be proud of yourself, show warmth and dare to pursue what you want. The card encourages you to be both strong and caring, both decisive and open. When you love yourself and your passion, that energy spreads and attracts good things.
wands-queen.meaning_reversed: When reversed, confidence may waver, or the energy turns into jealousy, manipulation or a short temper. You may feel drained or selfish. The card reminds you to return to your self-worth and care for your emotions. Find joy and sincerity again, and avoid using your charm to control others.

love.upright: In love, the Queen of Wands suggests charm, warmth and confidence. Express yourself and love sincerely and warmly.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests jealousy or insecurity. Trust your own worth and communicate clearly.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages leading with enthusiasm, creativity and confidence. Lead and inspire your team.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a lack of confidence or excessive control. Listen to your teammates and rest.

study.upright: In study, you are confident, enthusiastic and an inspiration to others. Take the lead in a group, join activities and shine in the field you like.
study.reversed: Reversed, confidence may waver or you may be short-tempered under pressure. Stay calm and do not compare yourself with others.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests initiative, financial independence and confident decisions. Weigh things up and invest in what you love with a plan.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of spending to prove yourself. Be realistic and focus on your goals.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents vitality and confidence. Maintain your energy with movement and joy. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests low energy or pressure to always be radiant. Give yourself permission to rest.

wands-queen.symbolism: The queen sits on a throne decorated with lions, holding a sprouting wand and a sunflower, a symbol of vitality. The black cat at her feet suggests intuition and mystery. Her yellow gown stands for energy and warmth. The desert behind and the pyramids recall trials already passed. The card belongs to the element of Water within the suit of Fire, combining emotion and passion.
wands-queen.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: charm.

wands-king.name: King of Wands
wands-king.meaning_upright: The King of Wands is a leader with vision, full of enthusiasm and inspiration. The card suggests confidence, decisiveness and the ability to turn ideas into reality. You may be in a leading position or taking on a large project. Use your strength to encourage others, set bold goals and move forward with determination. This is a time for strategic action and for leading by example. You can achieve a lot when you combine passion with discipline.
wands-king.meaning_reversed: When reversed, power may be abused or you may be impatient. You may be domineering, hot-tempered or setting expectations too high. The card reminds you to listen, share decisions and balance vision with reality. Control your emotions and avoid imposing.

love.upright: In love, the King of Wands suggests a passionate, proactive and loyal person. Lead with respect and listen to the other person.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests control or a hot temper in the relationship. Soften and share decision-making.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages leadership, starting a business and turning vision into reality. Inspire and be decisive.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a rigid leadership style or conflict with superiors. Adjust and listen.

study.upright: In study, you have vision and the ability to lead. Set big goals, organize your work and be a model for your study group.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be domineering or setting expectations too high. Listen to feedback and adjust your goals to be more realistic.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests long-term vision and bold, calculated decisions. Keep discipline and manage risk.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of impulsive or arrogant decisions. Check information and listen to advice.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents vitality and the ability to motivate yourself. Keep steady habits. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests overwork or a hot temper affecting your health. Regulate yourself and rest.

wands-king.symbolism: The king sits on a throne carved with lions and salamanders, holding a sprouting wand, in an orange-red cloak. Salamanders, symbols of fire and transformation, appear on the robe and throne, recalling the power of change. The lion is courage and authority. The salamander on the cloak bites its tail, an endless cycle. The sky is a warm yellow. The card belongs to the element of Air within the suit of Fire, combining vision and action.
wands-king.miu: Wands are fire; Miu likes to warm up nearby but never touches it. This card reminds you: lead.

cups-ace.name: Ace of Cups
cups-ace.meaning_upright: The Ace of Cups is an invitation to open your heart to a new flow of feeling that is brimming over. The hand from the cloud lifts a cup overflowing with water, like a gift from the universe to your heart. The card signals an emotional beginning: love, friendship, reconciliation or a surge of creative inspiration. You are being called to listen to what you really feel and to allow yourself to love without rushing to judge. Receive gentleness, for yourself and for others. When your heart is open enough, you will notice the small beautiful things around you. This is a good time to share, to forgive and to nurture a sincere bond.
cups-ace.meaning_reversed: When the Ace of Cups is reversed, the flow of emotion may be blocked or bottled up. You may feel empty, withdrawn, or afraid of being hurt, so you close the door of your heart. You may also be giving too much and forgetting to fill yourself. The card asks you to stop and ask: what am I feeling, and what am I avoiding? Take time to care for your emotions, write down your thoughts or talk with someone you trust. Allow yourself to be sad, then gently open your heart again when you are ready.

love.upright: In love, the Ace of Cups suggests a beginning full of feeling: meeting someone who makes your heart flutter, or a deep renewal of feelings. Open your heart, show sincerity and let emotion guide you gently, while keeping the clarity you need.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are reluctant to open your heart, or feelings are bottled up in the relationship. Allow yourself to say what you feel and do not strain to hold everything inside.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests inspiration and satisfaction from work that suits your heart. Work involving care, creativity or connecting with people will nourish you. Follow what feels meaningful.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a lack of inspiration or feeling that work is draining you. Review what really nourishes you and make time to recharge.

study.upright: In study, a new love for a subject or field is blooming. Follow that inspiration, because learning that comes from joy tends to last.
study.reversed: Reversed, your feeling for study is running dry or being held back. Find again what once interested you and look after your spirits first.

finance.upright: In finances, the Ace of Cups suggests generosity and a feeling of enough. An opportunity may come through a relationship or a passion. Spend mindfully on what brings you joy and real meaning.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of spending to fill an emotional gap or giving too much. Tell emotional needs from financial ones so you can decide with a clearer head.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card encourages you to look after your feelings, meditate, journal and make time for joy. Drinking enough water and resting are also ways of loving yourself. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests bottled-up emotion or mental tiredness. Find a safe space to express yourself and do not hesitate to ask for support when needed.

cups-ace.symbolism: A hand from the cloud offers a cup marked with an M or a cross, with a white dove above carrying a wafer, symbolizing spirit and blessing. Five streams of water pour from the cup into a lake, the five senses or an overflowing stream of emotion. The lotus and leaves on the water suggest purity and the blooming of the soul. Water is a symbol both of the subconscious and of life. The Ace is the seed of the suit of Cups, belonging to the element of Water and representing love, intuition and emotion.
cups-ace.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: new feelings.

cups-2.name: Two of Cups
cups-2.meaning_upright: The Two of Cups is the card of sincere connection between two people. The two figures exchange cups in respect and understanding, symbolizing love, friendship or a balanced partnership. You may be meeting someone who makes you feel understood, or strengthening an existing relationship. The card emphasizes give and take, where both give and both receive. Be open, listen and value your differences. This is a good time to cooperate, to reconcile or to begin a commitment built on trust. Harmony arrives when two hearts turn toward each other.
cups-2.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the balance in a relationship may be wobbling. Misunderstandings, a lack of communication or differing expectations leave the two of you distant. One person may also be giving more than they receive. The card reminds you to talk frankly, look at what is missing and find ways to mend things. If the relationship no longer suits, part respectfully. Remember that harmony takes effort from both sides.

love.upright: In love, the Two of Cups is one of the most beautiful cards: mutual attraction, understanding and commitment. You may meet someone in tune with you, or your current relationship deepens. Cherish it and stay sincere.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests misunderstanding, imbalance or emotional distance. Listen to each other, state your needs clearly and adjust together.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests good cooperation, lasting partnership or a deal that benefits both sides. Build trust and communicate openly with colleagues.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows disagreement in a collaboration or an unfair arrangement. Clarify roles and expectations and find common ground.

study.upright: In study, there is good cooperation with classmates, teachers or a mentor. Study in a group, exchange ideas sincerely and build trusting relationships.
study.reversed: Reversed, disagreement or a lack of chemistry in the group may arise. Speak plainly, listen to each other and redefine roles.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests balanced financial cooperation, such as pooling capital or sharing costs. Be transparent and agree clearly from the start to avoid misunderstanding.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of disagreement about money or an unclear agreement. Write down the terms and talk frankly.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you of the benefits of mutual support. Having a companion helps you keep good habits. Balance feeling and body. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from a relationship affecting your mood. Find a peaceful space and speak about what makes you uneasy.

cups-2.symbolism: A man and a woman face each other, each lifting a cup, wearing wreaths, showing exchange and respect. Above them is a winged lion's head over two entwined serpent staves, recalling the principle of healing and passionate strength in balance. The small house on the hill behind stands for the family hearth. The green background and bright sky suggest harmony. The card belongs to the element of Water, is tied to the number 2, the number of pairing, and is linked to the sign of the Crab.
cups-2.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: connection.

cups-3.name: Three of Cups
cups-3.meaning_upright: The Three of Cups is the image of three people raising their cups in celebration amid a bountiful harvest. The card speaks of friendship, shared joy and the support of community. You may be about to attend a gathering, an anniversary or a reunion with familiar people. This is the time to enjoy, share laughter and thank those who walk with you. Joy multiplies when shared, and connection makes you feel you belong. Make time for the people who make you feel at ease and like yourself. It is also an occasion to acknowledge shared achievements and to nurture friendship.
cups-3.meaning_reversed: When reversed, joy may go too far or gatherings may lose their real meaning. You may feel left out of a group, hear gossip or notice envy. You may also be exhausted from too much socializing. The card reminds you to choose sincere relationships, set boundaries and take time alone when needed. Remember that quality matters more than quantity.

love.upright: In love, the Three of Cups suggests shared joy, friends celebrating together or a relationship that begins from your social circle. Enjoy the fun and share your happiness with those you love.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests outside interference or jealousy. Keep the relationship private and speak plainly with whoever is involved.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals good teamwork, shared results and a positive atmosphere. Celebrate with your teammates and make use of your network.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows team conflict, gossip or too much socializing. Stay professional and focus on your goals.

study.upright: In study, a lively circle of friends, plenty of group activities and creativity. Use the strength of the group, but remember to keep study time serious.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may slip into too much partying or have arguments in the group. Balance fun and study.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests income from collaboration or spending on happy occasions. Enjoy in moderation and budget for get-togethers.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of overspending on parties. Control your spending and do not let social pressure affect your finances.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages social connection to lift your mood. Laughter and bonding are good for you. Stay moderate. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests tiredness from overdoing social life or from isolation. Balance fun and rest.

cups-3.symbolism: Three young women in long dresses and flower wreaths lift cups together in a field, with fruit and pumpkins on the ground, symbolizing harvest and abundance. They link arms in a circle, showing unity. The different colors of their clothes are diversity in harmony. The wreaths are joy and festival. The card belongs to the element of Water, is tied to the number 3 and is linked to Mercury in the sign of the Crab, suggesting emotional communication.
cups-3.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: celebrate.

cups-4.name: Four of Cups
cups-4.meaning_upright: The Four of Cups is the image of someone sitting under a tree with arms crossed, looking at three cups in front of him without noticing the fourth cup offered from a cloud. The card speaks of boredom, apathy or contemplation that may make you miss an opportunity. You may feel everything is bland, with no interest left even though you already have plenty. The card reminds you to stop, re-examine what you truly want and open your eyes to what is being offered. This time may be used for rest and self-reflection, but do not let the weariness drag on. Look for gratitude and a wider view.
cups-4.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you begin to notice opportunities and shake off apathy. You may have just realized what you missed, or feel ready to act again. You may also be returning to a forgotten passion. The card reminds you to use this wave of awakening, to verify what you want and to step out of passivity.

love.upright: In love, the Four of Cups suggests boredom, apathy or dissatisfaction. You may be overlooking someone who cares about you. Re-examine your expectations and talk honestly.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are waking up to new feelings or finding your closeness again. Open your heart and notice the good things you already have.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests boredom with work or a lack of drive. Review your goals, rest and look for new meaning. Do not overlook an opportunity knocking at your door.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you finding motivation again or noticing a new opportunity. Act and try something different.

study.upright: In study, you are bored or not yet interested, so you may miss the opportunity at hand. Stop and look at what is being offered to you.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are starting to shake off the sluggishness and are ready to take a new chance. Act while the motivation has just returned.

finance.upright: In finances, the card advises you to reassess what you have and not miss an opportunity out of indifference. Consider offers seriously.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are paying attention to financial opportunities again. Weigh things up and act when ready.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card asks you to notice feelings of boredom or low energy. Find a new activity and rest. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests energy returning. Keep up positive habits and connect with people.

cups-4.symbolism: A young man sits cross-armed, eyes closed or looking down, under a tree, with three cups lined up before him. A hand from a cloud offers a fourth cup that he does not seem to notice. His closed posture shows he is distant from the world. The tree is steadiness and shelter. The quiet landscape suggests reflection. The card belongs to the element of Water, is tied to the number 4, a number of stability but also of stagnation, and is linked to the Moon in the sign of the Crab.
cups-4.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: boredom.

cups-5.name: Five of Cups
cups-5.meaning_upright: The Five of Cups is the image of a figure in a black cloak looking down at three spilled cups while two cups still stand behind. The card speaks of sadness, loss and regret. You may be hurting over something that has passed, such as a relationship, an opportunity or an expectation that did not work out. This feeling is real and deserves respect. Still, the card also reminds you that there are full cups behind you. When you are ready, turn around and see what remains. There is no need to hurry; give yourself time to hurt and to heal.
cups-5.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you begin to recover, accept the loss and find hope again. You may forgive yourself or others and look toward the future. You may also still be clinging to the past. The card reminds you to value what is left and move on with the lesson you have learned. Healing comes bit by bit.

love.upright: In love, the Five of Cups suggests sadness from a breakup or an expectation that did not come true. Allow yourself to hurt, then look at the good that remains and the relationships still beside you.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are healing after a hurt and are ready to open your heart. Be patient and forgive yourself.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests disappointment over an opportunity or project. Learn from it and focus on what is still possible.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you getting over a failure and looking ahead. Use the lesson to prepare your next step.

study.upright: In study, you feel regret over a low grade or a failure. Allow yourself to be sad, then look at what remains and what you can still do.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are gradually accepting and getting back up after a setback. Take the lesson, share with someone you trust and move on.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests loss or disappointment about money. Learn from the experience, check what remains and plan a recovery.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are recovering financially. Keep up discipline and rebuild gradually.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card reminds you to allow yourself to be sad and to find support. Care for your feelings and rest. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are gradually recovering. Keep caring for yourself and stay connected with loved ones.

cups-5.symbolism: A man in a black cloak bows his head over three spilled cups, with red liquid flowing out, while two cups behind him are still standing. The river is the boundary between conscious and subconscious, and the bridge in the distance leads to a house, suggesting hope and a place to return to. The gray sky sets off the sorrow. His turned back to the two remaining cups shows his focus on loss. The card belongs to the element of Water; number 5 is the number of challenge, and it is linked to Mars in Scorpio.
cups-5.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: loss.

cups-6.name: Six of Cups
cups-6.meaning_upright: The Six of Cups recalls sweet memories, innocence and simple kindness. The image of two children exchanging a cup of flowers reminds you of warm moments from the past. You may meet an old acquaintance, remember your childhood or rediscover simple joy. The card encourages you to treasure beautiful memories and use them to nourish the present. It is also a time to share kindness without expecting anything in return. Let your heart soften and find your innocence again, but remember that you are living in the present.
cups-6.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be stuck in nostalgia or idealizing the past. You may also be maturing, letting go of old things to move on. The card reminds you to tell the difference between treasuring memories and avoiding the present. Learn from the past, but do not let it hold you back. Build something new on the good values of the old.

love.upright: In love, the Six of Cups suggests a tender relationship, long-standing affection or meeting an old flame. Treasure shared memories and build something new together.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are clinging to the past or to an ex. Look at things realistically and allow yourself to move on.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests former colleagues, a project tied to memories, or work with children or in education. Use your past experience and keep good relationships.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you clinging to old ways. Try new methods and widen your view.

study.upright: In study, old knowledge and familiar people will help. Review the basics, contact former teachers or relearn something you once loved.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be clinging to an old study method or living in nostalgia. Update your methods and look forward.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests generosity, or an inheritance or gift. Spend meaningfully and keep good traditions.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of clinging to an old way of managing money that no longer fits. Update your financial plan.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card advises you to find simple joys again, like a walk or playing with loved ones. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests nostalgia may be pulling you down. Find a new activity to refresh your spirit.

cups-6.symbolism: A boy offers a cup full of white flowers to a little girl in a quiet garden, with four other cups full of flowers set around. Flowers are a symbol of innocence and beautiful memories. The adult walking away in the background hints at the grown-up world. The house and stone column recall childhood safety. The bright colors give a feeling of warmth. The card belongs to the element of Water, is tied to the number 6 and is linked to the Sun in Scorpio.
cups-6.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: nostalgia.

cups-7.name: Seven of Cups
cups-7.meaning_upright: The Seven of Cups is the image of a figure standing before seven cups holding strange things that float in the clouds. The card speaks of choices, dreams and rich imagination, but also warns of illusion. You may have so many possibilities that it is hard to decide, or be swept up in beautiful things that may not be realistic. Enjoy your creativity, but also decide what is truly worth chasing. When you pick a direction and act, your dreams have a chance to become real.
cups-7.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the fog begins to lift and you see your choices more clearly. You can decide, focus on one direction and wake from the illusion. You may also still be confused by too many things. The card reminds you to assess reality, remove options that do not fit and commit to what has meaning.

love.upright: In love, the Seven of Cups suggests many options or illusions about the other person. Look at reality and ask yourself what you really want before committing.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are seeing the relationship more clearly and are ready to choose. Speak honestly and act consistently.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests many attractive directions. Define your goal and filter, avoiding scattering. Put your dreams into a concrete plan.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you focusing and choosing a clear direction. Start taking action.

study.upright: In study, you have too many choices and tend to daydream. Write down the directions, compare them realistically and choose one to pursue.
study.reversed: Reversed, you begin to see your realistic goal and hesitate less. Turn ideas into a concrete plan.

finance.upright: In finances, the card warns of the illusion of getting rich quick or too many investment options. Research carefully and choose what fits.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you see financial opportunities more clearly. Decide on the basis of data and discipline.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you not to escape reality through daydreams or unhealthy habits. Keep realistic routines. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are becoming clearer-headed. Keep up clear, healthy habits.

cups-7.symbolism: A silhouette with its back turned stands before seven cups floating on clouds, each holding something: a face, a snake, a castle, jewels, a laurel wreath, a dragon and a covered shadow. These represent temptation, power, money, victory and fear. The clouds show they are only imagination. The card belongs to the element of Water, number 7 is a trial, and it is linked to Venus in Scorpio.
cups-7.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: illusion.

cups-8.name: Eight of Cups
cups-8.meaning_upright: The Eight of Cups is the image of a figure turning his back on eight neatly stacked cups and walking toward the mountains under the moonlight. The card speaks of leaving what no longer brings meaning, even though on the surface things are fine. You may feel that something deeper is missing and decide to go looking for it. This is a journey of awakening, letting go and seeking what truly matters. Though not easy, the decision comes from a clear awareness of your own needs. Trust your intuition, and allow yourself to walk.
cups-8.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may hesitate to leave, delay, or return to the old. You may also be clinging to the familiar for fear of the unknown. The card asks you to see what is holding you back and whether it is still right for you. Be honest with yourself, and if need be, prepare well before you go.

love.upright: In love, the Eight of Cups suggests leaving a relationship that has lost its meaning, or seeking something deeper. Respect your feelings and communicate sincerely.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are hesitating to leave or trying to save things. Think carefully about what you truly need.

career.upright: In your career, the card hints that you want to change direction and leave work that no longer has meaning. Prepare well and look for something that fits your values.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you clinging to an old job for fear of change. Reassess and make a safe plan.

study.upright: In study, you feel your current way of learning or major no longer fits. It may be time to leave in search of something more meaningful, but weigh it carefully.
study.reversed: Reversed, you hesitate between staying and going, or return to what you dropped. Be clear about what you really need before you decide.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests giving up an investment or lifestyle that does not fit. Consider it carefully so that change is prepared.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of clinging to the old way or delaying adjustments. Review and act when you are ready.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card suggests a need for rest and leaving a stressful environment. Listen to your own needs. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are putting off self-care. Make time to rest and seek support.

cups-8.symbolism: A figure with a staff turns away, walking between rocky mountains and water, leaving behind eight neatly stacked cups, with one in the middle missing, meaning what is lacking. Above is a moon with a face, half full and half crescent, suggesting intuition and transition. The red cloak and red boots show resolve. The flowing river is emotion. The card belongs to the element of Water, number 8 is transition, and it is linked to Saturn in Pisces.
cups-8.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: let go.

cups-9.name: Nine of Cups
cups-9.meaning_upright: The Nine of Cups is known as the wish card. The man sits contented before nine cups lined up behind him, showing satisfaction and results. You may be getting what you hoped for, or feeling grateful for your life. Enjoy it, celebrate and share your joy. The card reminds you to value what you have and let yourself feel full. At the same time, remember that true satisfaction comes from within, not only from material things.
cups-9.meaning_reversed: When reversed, satisfaction may be shallow or a wish unfulfilled. You may be chasing material things and still feel lacking, or be too self-satisfied. The card asks: what truly makes me happy? Find joy in simple things and do not compare yourself with others.

love.upright: In love, the Nine of Cups suggests contentment, happiness and a relationship that leaves you feeling fulfilled. Treasure it and show gratitude.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests dissatisfaction or expectations that are too high. Talk and find joy in what is real.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals success, satisfaction with your work or reaching a goal. Celebrate the results and keep your drive.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows success that is not complete or a lack of meaning. Reconsider what you truly want.

study.upright: In study, you are satisfied with your results and what you have achieved. Reward your effort and keep the joy of learning.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be complacent or the results are not satisfying. Set more meaningful goals instead of just seeking comfort.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests stability and satisfaction. Enjoy the results and spend meaningfully.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of spending to fill an emotional void. Find joy that does not depend on material things.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents contentment and balance. Keep a healthy lifestyle and enjoy it. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests excessive habits. Be moderate and find healthy joys.

cups-9.symbolism: A well-fed man in a red hat sits with arms folded on a wooden bench, with a table covered in blue cloth behind him and nine cups arranged in an arc. His relaxed posture shows contentment. The warm yellow background stands for prosperity. The card belongs to the element of Water, number 9 is near completion, and it is linked to Jupiter in Pisces, the planet of good fortune.
