cups-9.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: contentment.

cups-10.name: Ten of Cups
cups-10.meaning_upright: The Ten of Cups is the image of a happy family beneath a brilliant rainbow. The card speaks of emotional fulfillment, a warm home and harmony. You may feel that you belong, are loved and are safe. This is the result of a long emotional journey. Treasure your loved ones, share your joy and build an environment full of warmth. The card encourages you to live by the values you believe in and to enjoy this completeness.
cups-10.meaning_reversed: When reversed, happiness may be incomplete, or there may be conflict in the family or community. You may also be chasing someone else's picture of happiness. The card reminds you to talk, to mend, and to define what real happiness means to you.

love.upright: In love, the Ten of Cups suggests a lasting, happy and fulfilling relationship. It may involve a long-term commitment or building a family.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests discord or expectations that do not fit. Talk openly and mend things step by step.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests a harmonious work environment and achievements that carry meaning. Build a positive culture.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows conflict in the team or a lack of satisfaction. Improve communication and shared values.

study.upright: In study, the learning environment is harmonious, your family is supportive and you are happy with your path. Appreciate that support.
study.reversed: Reversed, family expectations or disagreement may cause pressure. Talk sincerely about what you want.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests stability for the family and a sense of security. Make long-term plans for those you love.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial disagreement in the family. Communicate transparently and set shared goals.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card represents good mental health through connection. Keep in touch with your loved ones. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from family or loneliness. Seek support and say what you need.

cups-10.symbolism: A couple with arms around each other and two children dancing look up at ten cups forming a rainbow in the sky. The house on the hill, the river and the trees are prosperity and peace. The rainbow is the promise after the rain, the harmony of emotion. The card belongs to the element of Water, number 10 is completion, and it is linked to the planets in Pisces, the place of union.
cups-10.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: family.

cups-page.name: Page of Cups
cups-page.meaning_upright: The Page of Cups is a gentle, imaginative young person who always listens to the voice of the heart. The card often brings a small but warm message: an invitation, good news, or a creative idea that suddenly surfaces like a fish popping out of a cup. You may be starting to explore your emotional world, trying a new art form or opening up to a young relationship. Keep your curiosity and do not be afraid to appear soft, because sensitivity is the gift that helps you understand yourself and others. Let intuition guide you, jot down dreams or passing ideas, and allow yourself to play with beautiful things. What matters is acting gently and sincerely and letting feelings unfold at their own pace.
cups-page.meaning_reversed: When the Page of Cups is reversed, sensitivity can become excessive or emotions can swing so much that it is hard to hold your ground. You may be daydreaming to the point of avoiding reality, or receiving an unexpected message and feeling hurt. Your creativity may also be blocked by fear of judgment. The card reminds you to find balance between heart and reason: feelings deserve to be heard but should not be the only one at the wheel. Write down what you are feeling, talk with someone you trust and care for yourself gently. When you are steady enough, lovely ideas will return and may become real.

love.upright: In love, the Page of Cups suggests gentle romance, sweet messages or a new, tender flutter of feeling. Express your affection sincerely and keep a lovely innocence, but also notice whether both your feelings are moving together. A small, thoughtful gesture can open a door to closeness.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests moody feelings, unrealistic expectations, or idealizing the other person. A message may leave you sad. Slow down, ask directly what you need to know and do not let imagination fill the gaps the other person has not spoken.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a creative opportunity, a small offer or good news related to work in the arts, counseling or care. Experiment, learn from those ahead of you and trust your intuition when choosing projects. Your curiosity and genuine feeling are your own advantage.
career.reversed: Reversed, you may be unfocused because of emotions, or hesitant to share ideas for fear of criticism. Set concrete daily goals, separate personal feelings from work and ask someone trustworthy for feedback so your ideas can be refined.

study.upright: In study, you have a creative idea or a small piece of good news about your learning. Keep your curiosity, note down inspiration and try a new way to study.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are prone to daydreaming, oversensitivity or lack of focus. Tie your ideas to concrete action.

finance.upright: In finances, the Page of Cups suggests a small opportunity from a hobby or creativity, such as selling handmade goods or taking freelance work. Start at a moderate scale, keep clear records of income and spending, and let joy in your work nurture your perseverance, not just chasing numbers.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of spending on impulse from emotion or being drawn into a money-making idea that sounds attractive but lacks a basis. Wait a beat before large purchases, research carefully and do not let a passing mood decide your investments.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card encourages you to nurture your feelings through gentle activities such as drawing, writing, listening to music or walking by water. Allowing yourself to play is also self-care. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests easily shifting, easily hurt feelings or a vague anxiety. Keep a steady daily rhythm, sleep enough and say what is unsettling you to someone you trust instead of keeping it inside. If a heavy feeling lasts, seek professional support.

cups-page.symbolism: A young man in a tunic patterned with lotus flowers and a blue hat stands by the sea, holding a cup from which a small fish pops up as if talking with him. The fish is a symbol of an idea, intuition or a message from the subconscious, and his gentle surprise shows openness to the unexpected. The sea behind him is the vast world of feeling, and the gentle waves stress peace. The flower pattern suggests purity and slowly unfolding beauty. His slightly turned stance, half toward the sea and half toward the viewer, shows curiosity. The card belongs to the element of Earth within the suit of Water, representing a sincere learning of the emotions.
cups-page.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: good news.

cups-knight.name: Knight of Cups
cups-knight.meaning_upright: The Knight of Cups is a knight who brings his heart into the adventure. He advances slowly on a white horse, holding out a cup like a sincere invitation. The card suggests romance, thoughtfulness and beautiful ideals. You may receive an offer that comes from the heart, such as an invitation to meet, a creative opportunity or a reconciliation. You may also be the one bringing sincere feeling to someone or a project you believe in. Live by your values, communicate with gentleness and let kindness lead. Still, this knight also reminds you to keep your feet on the ground: a lovely ideal needs to be supported by concrete action so it is not only a dream.
cups-knight.meaning_reversed: When the Knight of Cups is reversed, romance can become unrealistic or moody. You may promise a lot but find it hard to keep your word, or be carried away by emotion and overlook reality. Someone around you may also be charming but lacking depth, leaving you disappointed. The card reminds you to check whether words go together with actions, and whether you are pursuing a real person or an ideal image. Balance heart and reason, say plainly what you need, and let sincerity, not only romance, lead the relationship.

love.upright: In love, the Knight of Cups is the image of a romantic suitor: thoughtful gestures, a gentle confession or a meaningful invitation. Receive it and respond sincerely, while observing whether the romance lasts over time and action.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests promises that are not yet firm, shifting feelings, or avoidance of commitment behind a charming surface. State your expectations, do not rush to place full trust, and let time show the consistency of the other person and of yourself.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a creative offer, an opportunity for artistic collaboration or work that lets you express your personal values. Pursue what feels meaningful, but prepare a concrete plan and take practical factors such as time and resources into account.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows an illusion about an opportunity, or emotion leaving you unfocused. A partner may be making empty promises. Ask for a clear written agreement and do not let outward appeal replace a real assessment.

study.upright: In study, you pursue your passion romantically and may receive an attractive invitation or offer. Weigh it carefully instead of only following your feelings.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be moody, idealizing or avoiding reality. Match your dreams against a feasible plan.

finance.upright: In finances, the Knight of Cups suggests an attractive offer or a money decision that comes from inspiration. Examine the terms closely, compare options and commit only when the numbers and your personal values both check out. Let the heart advise but let reason sign.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial promises that are too good, or spending to impress. Verify your sources, set a spending limit before parties, gifts or emotionally driven investment offers.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages caring for your mind through things you love, such as music, art or walks by water. Keep gentle habits and listen to your feelings. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests shifting emotions that affect your sleep and daily rhythm. Build steady habits, limit mood-altering substances and share with loved ones when you feel swept up in a wave of feeling.

cups-knight.symbolism: The knight wears silver armor, with a helmet and shoes bearing small wings that suggest the agility of the soul, and rides a white horse at a slow walk, holding the cup in both hands as if offering a message. The slow horse, unlike those of the other knights, stresses gentleness and intent. His cloak embroidered with fish signals a bond with emotion and the subconscious. The river flowing through the cool green scene is the stream of feeling that guides. The distant mountain stands for an ideal goal. The card belongs to the element of Fire within the suit of Water, combining action with emotion, so it carries a proactive, romantic energy.
cups-knight.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: romance.

cups-queen.name: Queen of Cups
cups-queen.meaning_upright: The Queen of Cups is the image of a woman seated at the water's edge, looking deep into a closed cup as if listening to what only intuition can hear. The card stands for empathy, gentleness and the ability to understand others without many words. You may be connecting deeply with your inner world, caring for someone close, or noticing feelings that had been forgotten. Trust your intuition, allow yourself to feel fully and accompany others by listening. At the same time, keep boundaries so that compassion does not turn into carrying everyone's feelings. When you take care of yourself first, your gentleness will be more lasting and sincere.
cups-queen.meaning_reversed: When the Queen of Cups is reversed, sensitivity may be excessive, so you are easily swept up in other people's moods or bottle up your own feelings. You may become dependent, sulky, or unconsciously use emotion to manipulate. You may also be drained from giving a lot without receiving. The card reminds you to set healthy boundaries and care for your emotions through nourishing habits such as rest, journaling and time alone to recharge. State your needs clearly instead of waiting for others to guess, and do not consider softness something to be ashamed of.

love.upright: In love, the Queen of Cups suggests deep gentleness, delicate care and the ability to sense each other's needs. Open your heart, listen and show affection through small gestures. A relationship blooms when both feel safe to share their most fragile parts.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests unstable emotions, jealousy or too much dependence on the other person. Return to nourishing yourself, express your needs clearly and avoid silent sulking. An honest conversation usually solves more than waiting for the other to understand without words.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages work based on empathy, such as counseling, education, health care, the arts or customer care. Use intuition together with facts, listen to your colleagues and create a warm work environment with boundaries.
career.reversed: Reversed, you may be exhausted from carrying other people's feelings or letting your emotions govern your work. Keep a professional distance, note down the limits of your responsibility and make time alone after emotionally draining work.

study.upright: In study, you learn through empathy and intuition, which suits helping professions, the arts and psychology. Trust your feelings and look after your spirits.
study.reversed: Reversed, emotions may overwhelm your studies or you may be worrying too much about others. Set boundaries and put yourself first.

finance.upright: In finances, the Queen of Cups suggests managing money by intuition and care for loved ones. Combine your gut feeling with a concrete spending sheet. Spending on what brings peace and connection may be worthwhile, as long as it does not exceed your means.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of money decisions made by mood or spending to console your feelings. Wait until you are calm before large purchases, consult someone you trust and do not lend or give beyond your means just out of compassion.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card stresses how much feelings matter to the body. Make time to relax, take a warm bath, meditate or be near water, and let yourself rest without guilt. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests that overflowing or bottled-up feelings are causing tiredness. Find your own space, say what you hold inside and build regular self-care habits. If an overwhelmed feeling lasts, do not hesitate to seek professional support.

cups-queen.symbolism: The queen sits on a throne carved with mermaids and little children, set right at the water's edge, where gentle waves touch the foot of the throne, symbolizing a close relationship with the subconscious. The covered cup, decorated like a small church, shows that her feelings are guarded and sacred, not rushed into display. She gazes deep into the cup, as if listening to an inner voice. Her pale blue gown suggests water and gentleness, and the multicolored stones at her feet are the delicate beauty of the inner world. The soft sky and quiet shore create a feeling of peace. The card belongs to the element of Water within the suit of Water, and so it is the crystallization of intuition and empathy.
cups-queen.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: empathy.

cups-king.name: King of Cups
cups-king.meaning_upright: The King of Cups is the one who masters the world of emotions without shutting it out. He sits on a throne amid a restless sea, yet stays calm, holding a cup and a scepter, a symbol of heart and reason combined. The card suggests emotional maturity, the ability to listen, to reconcile and to give wise counsel. You may be in a position where you need to stay calm in the storm and support others without losing yourself. Use compassion together with clear boundaries, communicate with diplomacy and trust your ability to manage your emotions. The true strength of the King of Cups is to feel fully while staying steady enough to choose how to respond.
cups-king.meaning_reversed: When the King of Cups is reversed, emotional balance may be wobbling. You may bottle up feelings until they explode, or on the other hand show moodiness and coldness. Someone may also be using emotion to manipulate, or you may be trying to seem fine while confused inside. The card reminds you to admit your real feelings instead of covering them, to find healthy ways to express them and to avoid controlling others through emotion. Make time for yourself, and talk with someone you trust or a professional if needed. Being honest with yourself is the first step to regaining your balance.

love.upright: In love, the King of Cups is a mature, steady partner who knows how to listen. Show care through consistent actions, settle disagreements with calm dialogue and let both of you express feelings safely.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests hidden feelings, a partner who is moody, or control through silence. Say plainly what you feel, set clear boundaries and do not accept patterns that use emotion to manipulate, even from yourself.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages leading with understanding, diplomacy and calm as pressure rises. Work in counseling, education, health care, the arts or managing people may suit you. Reconcile conflicts with fairness and openness.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a moody leadership style, a lack of transparency or avoiding conflict. Control your emotions at work, decide based on facts and ask colleagues for input to avoid hasty reactions.

study.upright: In study, you are calm and balanced between reason and feeling. Help your friends, find a wise mentor and learn with a steady mind.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be suppressing feelings or being driven by pressure. Share with someone you trust instead of keeping it inside.

finance.upright: In finances, the King of Cups suggests calm management based on long-term values and the security of loved ones. Combine intuition with data, avoid letting emotion drive big decisions and keep a reserve for stormy times.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of financial decisions driven by emotion or pressure from others. Wait until your mind is calm, seek professional advice and avoid commitments made out of kindness that go beyond your means.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card stresses that mental balance is the foundation of health. Keep habits of relaxation, meditation, gentle exercise and connection with loved ones. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests that bottled-up feelings are causing physical tension. Find healthy ways to express yourself, such as writing, talking or exercise, and do not ignore prolonged tiredness. Seeking professional support is a sign of strength, not weakness.

cups-king.symbolism: The king sits on a throne set amid a rough sea, with a fish leaping on one side and a ship sailing on the other, showing a full life moving around him while he stays steady. One hand holds a cup, the other a short scepter, symbolizing mastery of emotion and gentle power. The fish pendant on his chest recalls a bond with the subconscious. His blue and gold cloak suggests water joined with the light of wisdom. A clear sky surrounds the rolling waves. The card belongs to the element of Air within the suit of Water, joining reason with feeling, and so it is a symbol of emotional maturity.
cups-king.miu: A full cup of milk, Miu drinks; a cup full of feelings, Miu sits and listens. This card reminds you: calm.

swords-ace.name: Ace of Swords
swords-ace.meaning_upright: The Ace of Swords is the moment your mind suddenly clears. The hand from the cloud raises a sword through a crown, symbolizing the victory of intellect and truth. You may have just realized something important, found the answer to a long-running problem or had a fresh idea. The card encourages you to look straight at the truth and to use reason and clear words to cut through ambiguity. This is the time to make decisions based on accurate information, set clear goals and communicate honestly. Remember that the sword has two edges: truth needs to be spoken with kindness so that it heals instead of hurting.
swords-ace.meaning_reversed: When the Ace of Swords is reversed, clarity is clouded. You may be confused, short of information or having your judgment tilted by emotion. Your words, or someone else's, may be hurtful, or a good idea may not yet be clearly expressed. The card reminds you to slow down, gather more facts and check your assumptions. Write your thoughts on paper, talk with someone you trust and choose your words carefully. When your mind is calm, clarity will return.

love.upright: In love, the Ace of Swords suggests a frank conversation that clears things up, or a new awareness of what you need. Speak honestly, listen to the other person and let clarity lay the foundation for a more lasting relationship.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests misunderstanding, hurtful words or ambiguity in the relationship. Stop, clarify your intentions and avoid hasty judgment before talking.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a breakthrough idea, a clear decision or the start of a project based on sharp thinking. Use your focus to plan and present your views.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows unclear information or ideas that are not yet ripe. Check the facts, avoid hasty decisions and express yourself more clearly to colleagues.

study.upright: In study, a clear mind and a breakthrough idea. This is a good time to grasp the core of a problem, write an essay or make a clear argument.
study.reversed: Reversed, your thinking may be tangled or information unclear. Clarify the concepts first and do not conclude too fast.

finance.upright: In finances, the card advises you to look squarely at the numbers and make well-founded decisions. Read terms carefully, make a clear plan and rely on data more than emotion.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of inaccurate financial information or decisions made without thought. Verify your sources and ask a professional before committing.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you to look for reliable information and see your own habits clearly. A clear mind needs good sleep. For specific concerns, ask a healthcare professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a cluttered mind or information overload. Reduce exposure to sources of stress, rest enough and do not jump to conclusions from scattered information.

swords-ace.symbolism: A hand from the cloud holds a sword pointing straight up, its tip passing through a golden crown with a laurel wreath and palm leaves, symbolizing victory and fairness brought by reason. Six drops, or Yod letters, fall like sacred energy. The white-gray mountains below suggest the coldness and challenge of thought. The pale sky shows the clear stillness of Air. The Ace of Swords is the seed of the suit of Swords, belonging to the element of Air and tied to intellect, words, truth and decisions.
swords-ace.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: clarity.

swords-2.name: Two of Swords
swords-2.meaning_upright: The Two of Swords is the image of a blindfolded person holding two crossed swords across the chest. The card speaks of being torn between two choices or two sides that are hard to reconcile. You may be trying to keep the peace by avoiding feelings, or not have enough information to decide. This pause gives you a chance to weigh things, but it also reminds you that not choosing is itself a choice. Take off the blindfold, look at the truth you are avoiding, gather facts and listen to your intuition. When you dare to see clearly, the decision becomes lighter. Do not let fear keep you standing still for too long.
swords-2.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the stalemate may be broken. New information appears or you cannot delay any longer. You may also be overwhelmed by too many options, with anxiety rising. The card reminds you to face the truth, decide based on your values and accept that every choice has a trade-off. Ask for advice, but take responsibility for the final decision yourself.

love.upright: In love, the Two of Swords suggests hesitation, a lack of communication or hidden feelings. Drop your defenses, talk about what you feel and speak honestly to get out of the tug-of-war.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests the truth in the relationship gradually coming out, or you finally making a decision. Prepare yourself and put honesty first.

career.upright: In your career, the card shows you standing between two career choices or two sides with opposing views. Gather more information, weigh pros and cons and set a deadline for a decision.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you starting to choose a direction or feeling pressure to decide. Rely on facts and personal values; do not decide out of fear.

study.upright: In study, you are torn between two options and find it hard to decide. Gather more information, then dare to choose instead of avoiding.
study.reversed: Reversed, the indecision may drag on, or you are overloaded with information. Set a deadline for your decision.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests being torn between two options, such as saving or investing. Compare carefully, find advice and avoid delaying so long that you lose the opportunity.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests new financial information or that you are forced to choose. Evaluate calmly and decide on the basis of your long-term plan.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you not to avoid your body's signals. Gather reliable information and balance rest with action. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from prolonged indecision. Seek support, meditate or talk to ease anxiety and make a decision.

swords-2.symbolism: A woman in white sits on a stone bench, blindfolded, with two crossed swords held across her chest, symbolizing defensiveness and a closed-off heart. Behind her is a calm sea with jagged rocks, meaning suppressed feelings and hidden danger. The crescent moon in the sky suggests neglected intuition. The sky is clear and still. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 2, the number of balance and choice, and is linked to the Moon in Libra.
swords-2.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: stalemate.

swords-3.name: Three of Swords
swords-3.meaning_upright: The Three of Swords is the image of a heart pierced by three swords in the middle of rain. The card speaks of emotional pain, a truth that is hard to accept or a separation. You may be grieving a loss, hurtful words or an event that makes your heart tighten. This pain is real and deserves to be acknowledged. The card does not tell you to be strong right away; it reminds you to allow yourself to feel and to cry if you need to. After the rain, the sky gradually brightens. Look straight at the pain to understand where it comes from, and make time for healing. When you do not avoid it, the wound has a chance to heal fully.
swords-3.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the process of recovery begins, you slowly forgive and let the pain pass. However, the card may also show that you are suppressing sadness or holding on to an old wound. Care for your emotions, talk to someone you trust and forgive yourself. Do not force yourself to forget fast; let time do its work.

love.upright: In love, the Three of Swords suggests hurt, separation or a painful truth. Allow yourself to be sad, say what you feel and avoid harsh criticism while in pain.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are healing after hurt or forgiving. Keep taking care of yourself and open up when you are ready.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests disappointment, harsh conflict or bad news. Stay calm, draw a lesson and look for support. Do not let emotion push you into a hasty decision.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you getting over a hurt at work. Focus on what you can improve and set clear boundaries.

study.upright: In study, a disappointment such as a low grade, a harsh comment or failing an exam may hurt. Allow yourself to be sad, then draw the lesson.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are healing after a failure or still holding an old sadness. Let go and return to your goal.

finance.upright: In finances, the card may hint at a loss or bad news. Face the truth, make a recovery plan and avoid deciding while grieving.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are recovering financially. Be patient, learn from the experience and rebuild step by step.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card reminds you not to hide your sadness. Seek support, rest and say what you feel. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are slowly healing but need time. Keep up your self-care routine and do not hesitate to ask for help.

swords-3.symbolism: A red heart pierced by three swords floats against a gray sky with falling rain. The heart is feeling and love, the swords are the pain of thoughts and words. Rain and gray clouds stand for sorrow but also cleansing. There are no figures, which emphasizes that this pain is universal. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 3 and is linked to Saturn in Libra.
swords-3.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: heartbreak.

swords-4.name: Four of Swords
swords-4.meaning_upright: The Four of Swords is the image of a figure lying still on a stone tomb in a church, three swords hanging on the wall and one laid beneath. The card speaks of the rest that is needed after a stressful phase. You may need to stop to recover physically and mentally, to meditate, or to step away from the noise in order to think clearly. This is not laziness but preparation. When your mind is rested, you will return with new energy and a fresher view. Allow yourself to rest without guilt, because this stillness feeds your next step.
swords-4.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may not be letting yourself rest, or you rest while your mind stays restless. It may also be that you have rested enough and are ready to act again. The card reminds you to listen to your body, avoid burning out and find real ways to relax. If you feel yourself recovering, begin again gently, step by step.

love.upright: In love, the Four of Swords suggests a need for personal space or a pause to recover after tension. Say clearly that you need time.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are restless and cannot rest, or you are ready to return after a quiet spell. Open up and share what you have been thinking.

career.upright: In your career, the card advises resting after a stretch of overload, recharging and planning. Do not push yourself forward when you are exhausted.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you pushing on while exhausted, or being ready to return. Adjust your workload.

study.upright: In study, you need a break to recover from a stressful period. Pause, sleep enough and recharge before you continue reviewing.
study.reversed: Reversed, you have rested enough and are ready to return, or on the contrary have rested too long. Gradually return to your study rhythm in a gentle way.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests pausing new investments to observe and plan. Stay calm and do not act when your mind is tired.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are restless and eager to act. Make sure your decision rests on careful thought.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card emphasizes rest, sleep and meditation. Make time to recover. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests trouble sleeping, exhaustion or pushing yourself back too soon. Respect your body's pace of recovery.

swords-4.symbolism: A knight lies on a stone slab in a church, hands folded on his chest as if praying, three swords hung on the wall and one lying beneath the slab. The stained-glass window depicts a scene of healing or care, suggesting peace. Gentle light falls through it. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 4, foundation and rest, and is linked to Jupiter in Libra.
swords-4.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: rest.

swords-5.name: Five of Swords
swords-5.meaning_upright: The Five of Swords is the image of a winner holding three swords, smiling as two defeated people walk away. The card speaks of conflict, arguments and victory that comes at a cost. You may be facing a situation where winning means nothing if it costs affection or respect. Ask yourself what you are fighting for and whether it is worth it. The card encourages you to look back at your motives, choose battles worth fighting and sometimes let others win to keep the peace. True victory is when everyone keeps their dignity.
swords-5.meaning_reversed: When reversed, conflict may ease and lead to reconciliation. You may feel regret over your words or decide to let an argument go. The card may also hint at avoiding a conflict that needs solving. Admit your share of the fault and look for a fair solution. Forgiveness lightens both sides.

love.upright: In love, the Five of Swords suggests quarrels and win-or-lose in a relationship. Avoid using words that hurt and look for ways to understand each other.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests reconciliation or regret after an argument. Apologize sincerely and speak calmly.

career.upright: In your career, the card warns of unhealthy competition or winning at the cost of colleagues' goodwill. Consider long-term consequences before acting.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you avoiding conflict or seeking reconciliation. Clarify the issue in a constructive spirit.

study.upright: In study, conflict, unhealthy competition or a win-lose feeling. Pick battles worth fighting and do not trade relationships for a few points.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may reconcile or regret a conflict. Apologize if needed and focus on what matters.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests money disputes or a short-term win that costs more than it gains. Negotiate fairly and keep the relationship.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are settling a dispute or letting go to keep the peace. Agree things clearly.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card points to stress from conflict affecting your mood. Find healthy ways to release it. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are slowly feeling lighter after conflict. Keep caring for your feelings and avoid creating more tension.

swords-5.symbolism: A young man with a smirk holds three swords, with two more lying on the ground, while two figures in the distance turn their backs and walk away disappointed. The chaotic sky with torn clouds shows the conflict still echoing. The sea and rocky hill behind show coldness. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 5, challenge, and is linked to Venus in Aquarius.
swords-5.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: win or lose.

swords-6.name: Six of Swords
swords-6.meaning_upright: The Six of Swords is the image of a boat slowly carrying a woman and child across the water, from rough waters to calm. The card speaks of transition, leaving difficulty behind for peace. You may be passing through a phase of change, carrying sorrow but moving toward somewhere better. Allow yourself to leave, taking the lessons and leaving the burdens you do not need. The journey may not be over, but the direction is right. Be patient, stay calm and trust that the waters ahead will be smoother.
swords-6.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may resist leaving or carry too much emotional baggage. You may also be stuck, unable to let go of the past. The card asks you to see what is pulling you back and whether you are prepared. Settle unfinished matters so the transition is gentler.

love.upright: In love, the Six of Swords suggests healing and leaving a difficult time together or alone. Let go of the old and step toward peace.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests difficulty letting go of the past or an unresolved relationship. Speak honestly about what you are carrying.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests a transition, leaving a stressful environment or traveling for work. Prepare well and move toward a better environment.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you stuck in an old environment. Reconsider your reasons and make a clear plan.

study.upright: In study, you are moving into an easier phase, such as a change of environment or passing a hard stretch. Move forward calmly.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may find it hard to leave an old problem or your journey is slowed. Be patient and settle what is unfinished.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests gradual stability after a hard phase. Keep adjusting and follow your recovery plan.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of clinging to old financial habits. Be ready to change.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card suggests recovery and moving toward a calmer phase. Keep healthy habits. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are carrying too much mental weight. Let go gradually and seek support.

swords-6.symbolism: A boatman poles a woman and child across the water, with six swords standing upright in the boat, symbolizing the burdens that travel along. The two sit with heads bowed, covered in cloth, as if enduring. Behind them the water is choppy, ahead it is smooth, showing the transition. The faint far shore is hope. The card belongs to the element of Air, number 6, harmony, and is linked to Mercury in Aquarius.
swords-6.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: transition.

swords-7.name: Seven of Swords
swords-7.meaning_upright: The Seven of Swords is the image of someone tiptoeing away from the camp with five swords, leaving two behind. The card speaks of strategy and cleverness but also of sneaking or deception. You may be using cunning to get through a situation, or suspect someone is not fully honest. Consider: is this way truly right? You may need smarter planning, but also need to check whether you are deceiving yourself. Long-term honesty usually lasts longer than short-term tricks. Act carefully and be clear about your purpose.
swords-7.meaning_reversed: When reversed, the truth may come out, or you begin to feel uneasy about an action. A sneaky strategy may be discovered. The card encourages confessing, correcting mistakes and choosing the honest path. If you suspect someone, verify before you accuse. Transparency frees you from the burden of secrets.

love.upright: In love, the Seven of Swords suggests a lack of honesty or secrets in the relationship. Consider trustworthiness and speak plainly if you have doubts.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests the truth coming out or a confession. Face it and make amends with sincerity.

career.upright: In your career, the card warns of covert competition, colleagues who are not transparent, or a need for skillful strategy. Keep your professional ethics.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows a secret coming out or you choosing honesty. Settle things directly.

study.upright: In study, pay attention to honesty: avoid cheating, shortcuts or concealing things. Someone in the group may not be transparent; rely on your own effort.
study.reversed: Reversed, the truth may come out or you want to make amends. Be honest and start over instead of covering up.

finance.upright: In finances, the card warns of the risk of being tricked or a lack of transparency. Check contracts carefully and keep your paperwork.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests the financial truth coming out. Seek professional advice and stay transparent.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you not to deceive yourself about your habits. Look at them honestly. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are recognizing what you have been avoiding. Face it and seek support.

swords-7.symbolism: A man quietly leaves a military camp holding five swords, with two still planted in the ground, glancing back. The colorful tents in the distance show the crowd and distraction of the other side. His sly smile suggests calculation. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 7, challenge, and is linked to the Moon in Aquarius.
swords-7.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: cunning.

swords-8.name: Eight of Swords
swords-8.meaning_upright: The Eight of Swords is the image of a blindfolded, bound person standing in a ring of swords. The card speaks of feeling trapped and helpless, though in truth many of the bonds come from limiting beliefs or fear. You may feel there is no way out, even though there is still space to walk through. Ask: what is binding me, and is it real? When you change your view, seek support and take responsibility, you can step out of the ring of swords. The first step is realizing you are stronger than you think.
swords-8.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you begin to untie yourself, see clearly and take back control. You may recognize a limiting belief or find support. The card encourages small steps, with no need to rush. You may still be afraid, but you have started to see the door. Trust your own ability.

love.upright: In love, the Eight of Swords suggests feeling trapped in a relationship or ruled by fear. Speak about your fear and seek support so you can see your choices clearly.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are regaining your freedom in matters of the heart. Be patient with yourself and set boundaries.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests feeling stuck, with few choices. Reconsider your limiting beliefs and find ways to widen your options.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you seeing a new direction. Take small actions to change.

study.upright: In study, you feel trapped, stuck because of fear or limiting thoughts. Realize that the way out may be closer than you think; ask your mentor.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are starting to shake off negative thinking. Keep taking small actions and trust your ability.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a feeling of being stuck or anxious. Review your options, seek advice and plan step by step.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are regaining control of your finances. Keep up discipline.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you that anxiety and negative thoughts can leave you exhausted. Seek support and relaxing habits. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are coming out of a cycle of worry. Keep positive habits and ask for help when needed.

swords-8.symbolism: A woman in a red dress, blindfolded and wrapped in cords, stands among eight swords planted around her, her feet in waterlogged ground. A castle on a distant hill suggests safety that is out of reach. The loose bindings show that she could free herself. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 8, and is linked to Jupiter in Gemini.
swords-8.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: self-limits.

swords-9.name: Nine of Swords
swords-9.meaning_upright: The Nine of Swords is the image of a person sitting bolt upright in bed, hands covering the face, nine swords hanging above. The card speaks of anxiety, nightmares and the nagging thoughts that often rise in the night. You may be swept up in worry or guilt that goes beyond reality. Remember that many fears live in the mind and grow bigger when you are alone. Say it aloud to someone you trust, write down your worries and seek support when needed. You do not have to bear this alone.
swords-9.meaning_reversed: When reversed, anxiety may ease as you find support or see the cause clearly. You may also be bottling up your worry. The card reminds you to look after your mental health, rest and seek help if you need it. Fear often shrinks once it is spoken.

love.upright: In love, the Nine of Swords suggests anxiety, insecurity or regret. Share your worries with your partner or a close friend instead of keeping them inside.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are feeling lighter. Keep communication open.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests pressure and excessive worry. Rest, set priorities and ask for support.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows pressure easing or you finding a solution. Keep adjusting your work pace.

study.upright: In study, anxiety, sleeplessness and exam pressure are weighing on you. Share with someone you trust, rest enough and remember that worry is often bigger than reality.
study.reversed: Reversed, the worry is easing or you are starting to look for help. Keep healthy habits and do not hesitate to see a professional if needed.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests worry about money. List things concretely, make a plan and seek advice to reduce vague fear.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are regaining calm about money. Keep up your plan.

mind.upright: For emotional well-being, the card points to sleep and anxiety. Seek professional support if it lasts. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests gradual recovery. Keep caring for yourself and maintain restful habits.

swords-9.symbolism: A person sits up in bed, hands covering the face, with nine swords hung horizontally behind against a black background. The quilt embroidered with roses and astrological signs suggests inner life and memory. The carving on the bed shows a struggle between people. The darkness shows that fear lives in the night of the mind. The card belongs to the element of Air, is tied to the number 9, and is linked to Mars in Gemini.
swords-9.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: anxiety.

swords-10.name: Ten of Swords
swords-10.meaning_upright: The Ten of Swords is the card of the most painful ending: ten swords in the back, a black sky, but the horizon has begun to brighten. The card speaks of hitting rock bottom, a crisis, betrayal or an outcome you cannot rescue. You may be feeling exhausted, hurt, or aware that something has truly ended. The comforting thing is that once you have hit bottom, you cannot fall further. Acknowledge the ending, stop trying to save what cannot be saved and allow yourself to rest, to cry and to recover. The dawn behind reminds you that every dark night ends. A heavy lesson often paves the way for a truly new beginning, where you rise lighter.
swords-10.meaning_reversed: When the Ten of Swords is reversed, you are stepping out of the worst phase, gradually recovering and standing up. The card can also show that you are prolonging the pain by holding on to the victim role or replaying old drama, refusing to accept that it is over. Perhaps the worst has passed but you do not yet dare to believe it. Care for yourself step by step, ask for support and focus on what you can do today. Healing does not need to be perfect, only to continue.

love.upright: In love, the Ten of Swords suggests the painful end of a relationship or a feeling of being betrayed. Allow yourself to hurt, avoid trying to save what is over and make time to care for yourself. When the dust settles, you will see more clearly what you need for love in the future.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are recovering from emotional hurt and starting to feel lighter. Be patient, do not rush into a new relationship to fill the gap and keep learning to love yourself first.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a sudden ending such as losing a job, a project collapsing or a betrayal at work. Accept the truth, keep your dignity and draw the lesson. This may be the time to start over in a direction that suits you better.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you recovering from a career setback. Reassess your skills, widen your network and avoid returning to a place that burned you out just because it is familiar.

study.upright: In study, a stage ends suddenly, or there is a heavy sense of failure. Remember this is the bottom; from here you can begin again.
study.reversed: Reversed, you are recovering and looking back at the failure more calmly. Begin again with a better plan.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests loss or hitting bottom, perhaps a failed investment or a prolonged difficult situation. Look squarely at the figures, cut unnecessary spending and seek professional advice to plan a recovery step by step.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it suggests finances gradually stabilizing after a bad stretch. Learn from the experience, build an emergency fund and avoid repeating the decisions that led to the earlier loss.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card points to heavy exhaustion, especially mental. Truly rest, seek support from loved ones or a professional and do not try to look strong. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are recovering and regaining energy. Keep up regular self-care, increase gentle activity gradually and keep asking those who accompany you for support when needed.

swords-10.symbolism: A figure lies face down on the ground with ten swords along the back, a red tunic spread out like blood, a hand making a sign that recalls ritual. The scene looks harsh but holds several points of hope: the black sky turns golden-orange at the horizon, announcing dawn, and the still water below shows that all the chaos has stopped. The distant mountain suggests a trial passed. The number ten is the end of a cycle, so everything fragile has finally fallen. The card belongs to the element of Air and is linked to the Sun in Gemini, a reminder that after the extreme end of negative thought comes new light.
swords-10.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: endings.

swords-page.name: Page of Swords
swords-page.meaning_upright: The Page of Swords is a young person standing in the wind, holding a sword high, eyes curiously scanning everywhere. The card suggests mental energy: you may be learning something new, asking many questions, receiving news or having a sudden idea. This is the time for sharp observation, gathering information and speaking your thoughts frankly. Keep your curiosity, do not be afraid to ask what seem like simple questions and verify facts before drawing conclusions. The Page of Swords also reminds you that words carry weight: choose them carefully, communicate clearly and use your intellect to build rather than argue. When you combine quickness with a learning spirit, you will go farther than expected.
swords-page.meaning_reversed: When the Page of Swords is reversed, quickness can turn into talking too much, gossip or careless remarks. You may blurt out something that hurts someone, hear rumors or react in haste without enough information. Your ideas may also be insufficiently prepared and so hard to convince others with. The card reminds you to slow down, check sources, think before speaking and avoid sarcasm. Take time to prepare, listen more than you speak and treat feedback as a chance to learn.

love.upright: In love, the Page of Swords suggests lively conversations, getting to know each other through words and a need for intellectual understanding. Speak honestly, ask sincere questions and listen to the answers before drawing conclusions about each other.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests misunderstanding from words, sarcasm or gossip getting in. Avoid speaking when angry, ask the person involved directly and take time to explain what you mean to avoid unnecessary scratches.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals an opportunity to learn, research or a new idea at work. Prepare well before presenting, ask good questions and use your quickness to pick up new skills.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you need to be careful with what you say at work, avoid gossip and prepare better for meetings. Check facts, rewrite your points before sending and stay professional.

study.upright: In study, you are curious, eager to ask and want to learn many things. Ask questions and read widely, but verify information before you believe it.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may talk more than you do, or take in information carelessly. Check your sources and study in depth.

finance.upright: In finances, the card advises you to look into things carefully, read many sources and make plans based on reliable information. This is a time for research rather than big moves. Learn to manage money carefully and proactively.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of misleading financial information or decisions based on rumor. Verify with official sources, ask someone with expertise and avoid sharing financial details casually.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages you to look for information from trustworthy sources and keep a clear daily routine. Keep your mind alert with enough rest. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a mind overloaded with information or worry from reading conflicting sources. Reduce exposure to sources of stress, rest and avoid rushing to conclusions from scattered information online.

swords-page.symbolism: A young person stands on a windy hill, raising a sword as if testing the wind's direction, with hair and clothes flying and rolling clouds showing a turbulent day. Birds in the sky stand for thought and messages. The alert posture and far-looking eyes express observation. Trees bend with the wind, recalling the energy of Air. The other hand is lowered, as if ready. The card belongs to the element of Earth within the suit of Swords, and so it is the beginning of learning in the realm of thought.
swords-page.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: curiosity.

swords-knight.name: Knight of Swords
swords-knight.meaning_upright: The Knight of Swords is a knight rushing forward with sword raised, his horse charging through a strong wind. The card stands for speed, ambition and the decisiveness of the intellect. You may be acting fast to reach a goal, saying plainly what you think, or facing someone who does. This energy is very useful when you need to break through delay, settle a problem decisively or chase an opportunity without hesitation. Still, remember that speed needs a direction. Check whether the goal is right, whether your words might hurt others and whether you have enough information before charging ahead. When you focus and know how to regulate yourself, you can accomplish a lot.
swords-knight.meaning_reversed: When the Knight of Swords is reversed, decisiveness easily becomes haste, aggression or lack of thought. You may react too quickly, say something hurtful or dive into something unprepared. You may also be stalled by fear of acting, or facing someone hot-tempered and stubborn. The card reminds you to slow down, breathe and ask what is really driving you. Make a plan, listen to other opinions and choose words that carry respect. A slow step in the right direction is always better than running fast to the wrong place.

love.upright: In love, the Knight of Swords suggests directness, fast pursuit or forceful exchanges. Speak honestly but tactfully, respect the other person's pace and do not let arguments overwhelm feelings.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a hot temper, hurtful words or impatience in the relationship. Stop before you react, separate feeling from argument and apologize when needed.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a period of quick action, high ambition and the ability to solve problems decisively. Focus on clear goals, communicate directly and prepare well so that speed brings results.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows impulsiveness ruining plans, conflict with colleagues or a project rushed into without preparation. Pause, review the details and adjust how you communicate to keep your relationships.

study.upright: In study, you learn fast, with determination, and want to reach your goal right away. Keep your sharpness but do not rush past the details.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be impulsive, hasty or arguing sharply. Slow down and listen before you counter.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests quick decisions based on reason. Assess risk, examine the numbers closely and avoid being swept along by the market's speed. Ambition is good when paired with a plan.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of hasty or reckless financial decisions. Wait to verify information, set a loss limit and avoid big commitments when you are impatient.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you that you have abundant energy but may overdo it. Train with a plan, rest enough and avoid nervous strain. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests exhaustion from running too fast or constant tension. Slow your pace, breathe deeply, sleep enough and spend time away from screens so your nervous system can recover.

swords-knight.symbolism: The knight in silver armor gallops through a strong wind with raised sword, his white horse almost flying. The trees behind bend with the wind and thick clouds roll, all stressing the speed and force of the element of Air. His red cloak and reins show decisiveness. Butterflies and birds decorating his armor suggest intellect and transformation. He does not look around, only straight ahead, showing absolute focus but possibly a lack of observation. The card belongs to the element of Fire within the suit of Air, combining action with thought.
swords-knight.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: determination.

swords-queen.name: Queen of Swords
swords-queen.meaning_upright: The Queen of Swords is a woman seated on a throne under the high sky, holding a sword upright in one hand and extending the other as if inviting the truth. The card stands for a keen mind, independence and the ability to say plainly what needs to be said. She has often gone through loss and so understands the value of honesty and boundaries. You may need to look at a situation objectively, state clearly what you want, or hold your position without being swayed by emotion. Listen to reason, ask sharp questions and present your case coherently. At the same time, remember to keep empathy so that directness does not turn cold. Clarity together with kindness is the strength of the Queen of Swords.
swords-queen.meaning_reversed: When the Queen of Swords is reversed, sharpness can become bitterness or criticism, and independence can turn into isolation. You may be closing off your feelings because you were once hurt, using words as weapons, or being too harsh on yourself and others. You may also meet a cold, judgmental person. The card reminds you to face the old pain, soften and listen. Keep your boundaries but do not build the walls too high. When you let empathy walk alongside reason, your relationships will be warmer.

love.upright: In love, the Queen of Swords suggests honesty, clear boundaries and a wish for a relationship based on respect for the mind. Say what you need in a calm voice, listen to the other person and do not let old wounds govern how you love.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are closing your heart, being harsh or using sharp words to defend yourself. Allow yourself to be a little vulnerable, share your feelings and recognize that not everyone is a threat.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages objective assessment, clear communication and decisions based on facts. You may excel in work that needs analysis, evaluation, writing or legal knowledge. Keep fairness and discipline.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows harsh criticism, inflexibility or isolation at work. Use feedback constructively, listen to colleagues and do not let past experience make you bitter.

study.upright: In study, you are clear, independent and good at critical thinking. Focus, say plainly what you do not understand and remove what distracts you.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be too harsh or closed off. Be gentler with yourself and ask others for support.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests level-headed management based on information and not driven by emotion. Make a clear budget, read terms closely and decide with objectivity.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of excessive strictness or rigidity that makes you miss opportunities. Be more flexible, listen to advice and avoid decisions based on old disappointment.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages disciplined habits and clear thinking about your body's needs. Look for reliable information and respect your own limits. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from over-control or negative thinking. Relax, share with someone you trust and remember that rest is also part of discipline.

swords-queen.symbolism: The queen sits on a throne carved with butterflies and angels, the sword raised straight to stand for truth and justice, her left hand extended as if ready to listen. The high sky, white clouds and flying birds suggest open-minded thinking. Her face is slightly turned, showing a sharp gaze but not a cold one. The white cloak embroidered with clouds and the butterfly crown signify transformation through wisdom. A distant tree on one side represents experience. The card belongs to the element of Water within the suit of Air, combining emotion that has been tested with sharp reason.
swords-queen.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: sharpness.

swords-king.name: King of Swords
swords-king.meaning_upright: The King of Swords is a leader who relies on intellect, principle and fairness. He sits majestically on his throne, sword upright, with a clear gaze unswayed by passing emotion. The card stands for sound decisions, coherent communication and the ability to assess a situation objectively. You may be in a position where you must make a judgment, set standards or resolve a dispute. Rely on facts, hold to principle and say clearly what needs to be said. The authority of the King of Swords lasts when it comes with ethics and respect. Use your intellect to serve what is right, not only to win.
swords-king.meaning_reversed: When the King of Swords is reversed, authority may be abused, becoming domineering, cold or manipulating through argument. You may meet someone who uses knowledge to impose, or you yourself may be too rigid and lacking empathy. Someone may also be distorting the truth. The card reminds you to check your motives, listen to other views and return to fairness. Set standards but do not lose your humanity. If you are the one under pressure, record events, stay calm and find support when needed.

love.upright: In love, the King of Swords suggests a relationship built on honesty, respect for the mind and clear communication. Speak truthfully with kindness, agree on shared rules and do not shy from discussing hard topics.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests coldness, control or using logic to win instead of understanding. Soften, listen to each other's feelings and remember that a relationship is not a debate.

career.upright: In your career, the card encourages leading on principle, deciding with facts and communicating coherently. Work involving law, analysis, management, education or counseling may suit you. Stay fair when evaluating others.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows abuse of power, lack of transparency or a rigid management style. Check your motives, make criteria public and listen to your team so that decisions are fairer.

study.upright: In study, you have logical thinking and good analysis and may be the one who makes the right call. Study systematically and use tight reasoning.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be too rigid or using reason to impose. Be open to other viewpoints and fairer.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests disciplined management, decisions based on reason and a clear understanding of contracts and rules. Read terms carefully, make a concrete plan and consult a professional when needed.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of misleading information, contracts lacking transparency or people using knowledge to manipulate. Verify, keep documents and seek independent advice before you sign.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages clear thinking about your habits, finding trustworthy information and keeping steady discipline. A clear mind needs sleep and rest. For specific health concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from over-control, mental overload or rigid thinking. Relax, move gently and share with someone you trust so that your mind can rest.

swords-king.symbolism: The king sits on an imposing throne, looking straight ahead, holding a sword upright, in a blue cloak embroidered with clouds. The throne carved with butterflies and small angels recalls transformation and the soul walking beside the intellect. The clear sky, white clouds and flying birds show a far-reaching view. The crown with a butterfly shape suggests humane wisdom. His steady seated posture shows calm. The card belongs to the element of Air within the suit of Air, and so represents pure reason and authority based on truth.
swords-king.miu: Swords are very sharp, Miu only uses claws. Speak gently. This card reminds you: reason.

pentacles-ace.name: Ace of Pentacles
pentacles-ace.meaning_upright: The Ace of Pentacles is the promise of a practical, lasting beginning. The hand from the cloud offers a gold coin in a green garden, like a gift of earth and sky to you. The card signals an opportunity in work, finances, health or a project that can take root and grow. This is a time to plant seeds with concrete action: make a plan, learn a skill, invest your time. You do not need results right away, only a firm foundation. Be grateful for what you have, tend it regularly and give time for the tree to grow. True prosperity begins with small habits repeated each day.
pentacles-ace.meaning_reversed: When the Ace of Pentacles is reversed, an opportunity may be delayed or you may not have noticed it. You may lack a plan, act in haste or focus too much on material gain. Fear of scarcity may also keep you from beginning. The card reminds you to revisit your foundation, make your goals practical and prepare carefully. Do not overlook small opportunities, because many big things start there.

love.upright: In love, the Ace of Pentacles suggests a solid beginning: a relationship with lasting potential or new stability. Show affection through actions and build trust.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of foundation or putting material things ahead of feeling. Talk about shared goals and lay the groundwork steadily.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals a job opportunity, a new project or practical advancement. Invest in your skills, make a plan and prepare your steps firmly.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows an opportunity delayed or poorly prepared for. Review your plan and be patient while building the base.

study.upright: In study, a practical opportunity such as a scholarship, a course or resources is opening. Take it and lay a firm foundation for what you want to build.
study.reversed: Reversed, an opportunity may be missed or resources may fall short. Make a financial plan and be more realistic before beginning.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests a new source of income, a wise investment or a chance to save. Start with small steps, set clear goals and increase gradually with discipline.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of hasty financial decisions or a shaky plan. Verify and avoid commitments beyond your means.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages building healthy habits such as regular meals and gentle movement. Persist in small steps. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests irregular habits or neglecting your body. Set realistic goals and keep them going.

pentacles-ace.symbolism: A hand from the cloud holds up a gold coin engraved with a five-pointed star, symbolizing the four elements plus spirit and practical prosperity. The garden below blooms with white lilies and red roses, a symbol of purity and passion nurtured. An arch of flowers leads to distant mountains, hinting at the journey ahead. The cloud is the unseen source of opportunity. The Ace of Pentacles is the seed of the suit of Pentacles, belonging to the element of Earth and tied to money, work, the body and matter.
pentacles-ace.miu: Miu does not understand money, but storing dried fish? Miu is great at that. This card reminds you: a practical opportunity.

pentacles-2.name: Two of Pentacles
pentacles-2.meaning_upright: The Two of Pentacles is the image of a person juggling two coins joined by an infinity loop amid rolling waves. The card speaks of the ability to balance many things at once and to adapt to change. You may be juggling work and family, money and time, or two opportunities. Stay flexible, keep your rhythm and do not try to do everything at once. Break up your priorities, set limits and enjoy the process. When you go with the flow instead of fighting it, you keep your balance amid the turbulence.
pentacles-2.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be overloaded, off balance or letting everything get tangled. You may have taken on too much or lack clear priorities. The card asks you to stop, list what matters and let go of what you do not need. Ask for support and rearrange your schedule. Balance does not mean perfection; it means adjusting continuously.

love.upright: In love, the Two of Pentacles suggests balancing feelings with other responsibilities. Make time for quality moments and talk about both of your needs.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are so busy that you forget the relationship. Prioritize the one you love and adjust your schedule.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests juggling several roles or projects. Stay organized, flexible and clear about priorities.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows work overload. Hand some off, say no gently and set limits.

study.upright: In study, you are juggling several subjects or studying while working. Set flexible priorities and manage your time carefully.
study.reversed: Reversed, you may be overloaded or your schedule is in a tangle. Cut back, ask for support and do not try to carry everything at once.

finance.upright: In finances, the card encourages flexible budgeting and balancing income and spending. Track your cash flow and adjust when things change.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of spending out of control or piling debt. Review your budget and seek advice.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you to balance work and rest. Keep a steady routine. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests overload and tiredness. Rest and reduce your tasks.

pentacles-2.symbolism: A young man dances on the ground, juggling two coins connected by an infinity loop. The restless sea behind with two ships bobbing shows the ups and downs of life that he still keeps pace with. His tall hat and red and blue clothes suggest cheerfulness and flexibility. The card belongs to the element of Earth, is tied to the number 2, balance, and is linked to Jupiter in Capricorn.
pentacles-2.miu: Miu does not understand money, but storing dried fish? Miu is great at that. This card reminds you: balance.

pentacles-3.name: Three of Pentacles
pentacles-3.meaning_upright: The Three of Pentacles is the image of a stonemason working in a church together with an architect and a monk. The card speaks of cooperation, professional skill and building something of value. You may be joining a team project, receiving feedback or sharpening your craft. Each person contributes a different piece of expertise, and the result is good when everyone moves toward a shared goal. Listen, learn and contribute fully. Quality work is recognized, and sincere cooperation produces more than one person alone could.
pentacles-3.meaning_reversed: When reversed, coordination may run into trouble. There may be poor communication, clashing roles or work that falls short of quality. The card asks you to clarify the shared goal, listen and improve your skills. Do not ignore feedback; use it to progress.

love.upright: In love, the Three of Pentacles suggests building the relationship together through shared effort. Cooperate, share responsibility and respect each other.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests disagreement about roles or a lack of effort from one side. Talk frankly.

career.upright: In your career, the card signals effective teamwork, recognized skills or an apprenticeship. Contribute your expertise and take in feedback.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows team conflict or low quality. Improve communication and process.

study.upright: In study, teamwork and learning from people with expertise are very effective. Cooperate, accept feedback and build practical skills.
study.reversed: Reversed, the group lacks coordination or quality falls short. Assign roles clearly and be willing to accept critique.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests income from skills and collaboration. Invest in expertise and build your reputation.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of a lack of a shared plan or financial disagreement. Clarify the agreement.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card encourages working with professionals and building lasting habits. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests a lack of support or inconsistent habits. Find someone to go along with you.

pentacles-3.symbolism: A craftsman stands on a bench working in a church, with three coins carved into the arch, beside an architect and a monk holding plans. The three figures stand for skill, plan and purpose. The stone vault is the shared work. The card belongs to the element of Earth, is tied to the number 3, and is linked to Mars in Capricorn.
pentacles-3.miu: Miu does not understand money, but storing dried fish? Miu is great at that. This card reminds you: cooperation.

pentacles-4.name: Four of Pentacles
pentacles-4.meaning_upright: The Four of Pentacles is the image of a person sitting clutching a coin, two coins under the feet and one on the head. The card speaks of the need for security and control over possessions. You may be holding on to what you have, saving, or protecting your resources. This is good when it brings stability, but taken too far it can become stinginess or fear of loss. Ask yourself whether you are gripping tightly out of fear, and whether you could loosen up a little. The best stability is when you both preserve and stay open to the flow.
pentacles-4.meaning_reversed: When reversed, you may be loosening your control or sharing more generously. You may also be overspending, or on the contrary being greedy and obsessed with material things. The card reminds you to find balance between keeping and giving. Review your relationship with money and security.

love.upright: In love, the Four of Pentacles suggests conservatism, fear of loss or difficulty opening up. Loosen up a little and share your feelings.
love.reversed: Reversed, it suggests you are learning to let go of control. Trust and be open.

career.upright: In your career, the card suggests stability, protecting your position and conserving resources. Be careful but do not miss opportunities by being overcautious.
career.reversed: Reversed, it shows you loosening control or sharing resources. Keep a balance.

study.upright: In study, you hold tight to your habits and existing knowledge. This brings stability, but do not be too conservative or afraid to try new ways.
study.reversed: Reversed, you loosen control, or on the contrary are too frugal about investing in learning. Balance it and invest reasonably in yourself.

finance.upright: In finances, the card suggests saving, holding on to money and financial security. Save with a plan but do not be too strict.
finance.reversed: Reversed, it warns of uncontrolled spending or excessive stinginess. Find a balance.

mind.upright: For well-being, the card reminds you not to over-control yourself. Balance discipline with relaxation. For specific concerns, ask a professional.
mind.reversed: Reversed, it suggests stress from over-control. Loosen up.

pentacles-4.symbolism: A man wearing a crown sits before a city, clutching a coin to his chest with two more under his feet, symbolizing holding on. The crown and cloak show status. The city behind is the society he has set himself apart from. The card belongs to the element of Earth, is tied to the number 4, stability, and is linked to the Sun in Capricorn.
pentacles-4.miu: Miu does not understand money, but storing dried fish? Miu is great at that. This card reminds you: safekeeping.

pentacles-5.name: Five of Pentacles
pentacles-5.meaning_upright: The Five of Pentacles is the image of two people wandering in the cold snow, one on crutches, one with a shawl over the head, passing by the stained-glass window of a warm, lit church. The card speaks of a phase of lack, which may concern money, health, love or a feeling of being abandoned. You may be worried about the future, lonely in your difficulties or feeling you are not enough. This hardship is real and deserves respect. What is notable is the warm light right beside them: help may be very close, but worry and pride keep us from lifting our heads. Dare to ask for support, look for community and remember that asking for help is a sign of courage. Every winter will pass.
pentacles-5.meaning_reversed: When the Five of Pentacles is reversed, the situation begins to brighten. You find help, a chance to recover or realize you have come through the worst. You may still worry about scarcity even though things are settling, or refuse help out of pride. The card reminds you to treasure those who held you up and keep building step by step. When you are steady again, be ready to give help to others, because everyone needs a lit window at some point.
